title: King faces calls for apology, slavery reparations in Caribbean
summary: King Charles III faces renewed calls for a slavery apology and reparations on a visit to the Caribbean, as protesters demand: "Pay us what you owe us."
story: Britain's King Charles III continued his nine-day tour of the Caribbean Thursday under mounting pressure to issue a formal apology for the U.K. royal family's historic role in the transatlantic slave trade and to support calls for reparations.

Charles was to visit Guyana on Thursday before traveling to Antigua and Barbuda for a meeting of heads of state of British Commonwealth nations, where leaders are expected to discuss the legacy of slavery.
His tour began Tuesday in the Bahamas, where the king addressed hundreds of young Bahamians and acknowledged Britain's colonial past.

"Some of what is best in Bahamian culture today, the most joyful, the most hopeful, the most bright, was born out of darkness," he said. "It is only right that we should acknowledge the great suffering and injustices of the past in these islands and beyond, even as we rejoice in the successes of the present and build new opportunities for the future."
On Wednesday, the king embraced the country's vibrant culture, joining a colorful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau surrounded by performers in elaborate costumes and feathered headdresses.
But around the celebrations, protesters held placards declaring: "Pay us what you owe us," demanding compensation for Britain's involvement in centuries of transatlantic slave trade.
Charles' remarks appeared to do little to satisfy campaigners who have long called for a formal apology and reparations.

Speaking to The Guardian newspaper on Wednesday, Dr. Niambi Hall Campbell-Dean, chair of the Bahamas National Reparations Committee, dismissed the monarch's remarks as "hollow platitudes" and said, "we deserve so much more than what was offered."

Buckingham Palace has said Charles will not offer a formal apology for slavery, saying such decisions are for the British government, not the royal family, but that he will not shy away from broader discussions about the U.K.'s involvement.

Experts say the royals are concerned that issuing a formal apology could open the door to legal claims for reparations, potentially exposing the family, and/or the British government, to substantial financial demands.

"The reason why he doesn't go further is that he's aware [of] what it will mean to actually apologize, in terms of the legal obligation to make reparation," Esther Stanford-Xosei, a lawyer and reparations expert, told CBS News in 2023, as Charles' second son Prince Harry's book "Spare" acknowledged the family had profited from the slave trade.
Stanford-Xosei said the family feared a formal apology could end up costing the monarchy, "not only money, but status … He will be exposing the criminality of this institution."
Calls for reparations

Between the 15th and 19th centuries, approximately 5 million enslaved Africans were transported to the Caribbean, including more than 2 million to British colonies, where they endured brutal conditions working in sugar, coffee and cotton plantations.

Historians have documented the monarchy's direct involvement in the trade, including investments by King Charles II and his brother James in the Royal African Company, which trafficked enslaved Africans across the Atlantic.

When slavery was abolished across most of the British Empire in 1834, the government allocated £20 million ($23 billion in today's money according to one estimate) to compensate slave owners, but not the enslaved. The compensation was part of a political compromise that helped secure abolition's passage by British lawmakers.

Britain subsequently played a significant role in suppressing the international slave trade during the 19th century, deploying the Royal Navy and investing substantial resources in abolition efforts. Its West Africa Squadron seized more than 1,600 slave ships and freed approximately 150,000 Africans between 1808 and 1869. One study estimated that Britain's wider anti-slavery efforts cost the equivalent of 1.8% of its national income annually over that period.

The debate over reparations has intensified in recent years, particularly following the global Black Lives Matter protests in 2020, which prompted renewed scrutiny of Britain's colonial past and the royal family's historical connections to slavery.
Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley has been among the leading voices calling for reparations, including investment in education, healthcare and economic development.

Speaking to The Guardian, the head of the Caribbean Community Reparations Commission, Hilary Beckles, said people in the Caribbean wanted "proprietary justice, beginning with remorse" from British leaders.
She urged Charles to "dig deep within his consciousness" and to offer young people he meets on his visit "the empowerment that he would give to his own children."
Not everyone in the Caribbean supports the idea of direct reparations, however.

Rasheed Griffiths, a Barbadian economist, told CBS News that "Caribbean leaders have consistently refused to implement prudent fiscal policies over the last few decades, which has led to the decay of Caribbean economies. But instead of realizing they have all the power to turn these countries around they prefer to seek scapegoats."

"The calls for reparations from the U.K. are nothing more than Caribbean leaders attempting to externalize their own failures," Griffiths said. "It should not be taken seriously by anyone, least of all the U.K. public."
Charles previously described slavery as an "appalling atrocity" that "forever stains our history" during Barbados' transition to a republic in 2021.

During a Caribbean tour in 2022, heir to the British throne Prince William and his wife Kate also faced protests over slavery and demands for reparations. William expressed his "profound sorrow" and described slavery as "abhorrent," but stopped short of a formal apology.

Many of the Caribbean nations Charles is visiting are former British colonies and several, including the Bahamas and Antigua and Barbuda, remain constitutional monarchies, which, despite them having gained independence decades ago, makes Charles their official head of state.

title: CEO says plan is to file for bankruptcy after ending luxury never-ending cruise
summary: More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury U.S. cruise ship ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs.
story: More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury U.S. cruise ship that was on a continuous around-the-world voyage ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs.
Villa Vie Residences, the Florida-based operator of the MV Odyssey, said the war with Iran quadrupled fuel costs and forced it to suspend operations on Tuesday.

CEO Mikael Petterson told CBS News in a phone interview Wednesday that Villa Vie Residences was paying an average of $700 a ton for fuel before the war broke out in late February. Since then, it has been paying anywhere from $2,000 to $3,000 per ton.
The Odyssey uses between 700 and 800 tons per month in fuel, Petterson disclosed.
"When you divide it over 300 people on board, it's just backbreaking," Petterson told CBS News. "And this has been going on for nine months. We've tried to do everything we can do."
In a statement, Villa Vie Residences said the per cabin fuel costs rose from an average of $1,800 per month before the war to between $6,000 and $8,000.
The company was unwilling to pass those rising costs on to its passengers, Petterson said.

The Odyssey launched in October 2024 for a continuous around-the-world journey. At the time, passengers could become residents of the ship by purchasing a permanent cabin for several hundred thousand dollars. Some sold their homes to do so. At the time, they were given a 15-year minimum guarantee of residency aboard the Odyssey.

The Odyssey attempted to counter the spiking fuel prices by slowing down its itinerary and spending five or six days in each port "hoping that things would come to a close in the Middle East," Petterson said, but it wasn't enough.
"For us, when our monthly expenses go up from $400,000 to $2 million, where are we going to get the $1.6 million?" Petterson asked.
The Villa Vie Residences CEO said that the ship ran out of money as it searched for a financial partner, and the plan is now to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
"We've borrowed money, we've stretched our payrolls as far as we can, and we're at a point where it's just at a breaking point where we need capitalization," Petterson said.
Passenger Benjamin Schatz thought the MV Odyssey would be his forever home.
"Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz, a retiree, told CBS News.

CBS News met Schatz in April 2025 for a story featuring Villa Vie Residences. At that point, he had been living on the ship for about one year. On Wednesday, he was given just hours to pack up his life and leave.
Said Schatz: "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."

title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68, dozens injured
summary: Dozens of people were killed or injured when a high-speed train crashed into another train in central Spain, officials said.
story: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped in central Spain, derailing two cars and killing at least 68 people Wednesday morning, according to local authorities.

The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers continue searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies.
The crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, according to Spain's rail system operator ADIF. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

Padilla told state broadcaster TVE the accident was between two high-speed trains heading in the same direction from Madrid to Seville and that one ran into the tail of the other while it was stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track.

The accident involved a train from Spain's state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO. Trains from those two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January. Padilla said 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers were in the IRYO train.
"Today all of Spain is grieving," Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning.
Sánchez called for increased safety measures to restore confidence in a high-speed rail system that was once a source of national pride.
"It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year," said Sánchez, who faces a national election on Nov. 29.

Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the crash was caused by what he called the "inexplicable" order from a central command center for Spain's trains after a security system had failed. He said the train engineers were not to blame.

Puente said that at 8:30 a.m. the security system on a stretch of 63 kilometers (39 miles) stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop. But the central command told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, and it ended up colliding with the stopped IRYO train at 8:53 a.m.

Puente said the train should never have been told to start moving again since there was still a "stop signal" active on that line. And if it had, at least it should have been told to go at reduced speed.
Authorities were still studying information to see how fast the train was going, but it could have been at 200 kph (124 mph) for that stretch of the track, Puente said.
"I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts," Puente said.

The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by olive fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left carriages shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said that emergency workers were focused on rescuing survivors and bodies from the most damaged train cars.
"It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," García said.
One passenger said, "We were all thrown into the air." He said he was "reasonably OK" but that his friend was in much worse condition.
Passenger Ignacio Relaño was traveling on the RENFE train. He told state broadcaster TVE that the train had stopped momentarily on the line before it started again and then crashed into the IRYO.

"We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact," he said. "The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cell phones. Everything shook."

Another passenger recounted to Cadena Ser radio how she felt the train slam on the brakes and was thrown forward in her seat, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw body parts and trapped people covered in blood.
The mayor of the nearby town of Urda, Manuel Galán, told Spanish state broadcaster TVE that civil protection authorities had asked his town hall to prepare a sports pavilion to attend to passengers.

In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people. The January incident shook the confidence the European country has in its extensive high-speed rail network.

title: Selma Blair breaks silence, weeks after arrest for alleged assault
summary: Actress Selma Blair broke her silence Friday, weeks after being arrested for an alleged assault on flight attendants on a Delta flight.
story: Blair, walking with her service dog, is doing photo ops for fans at '90s Con in Connecticut. (Obtained by Fox News)
Selma Blair on Friday apologized following her arrest after an alleged altercation with flight attendants on a Delta flight earlier this month.

The 54-year-old actress said her lawyers advised her not to say anything because of the ongoing legal matter but added, "Not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life. And, so, to the people I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed, I am so sorry."
In the emotional Instagram video, taken in what appeared to be her home, she added that she would be taking care of her health and her son "and thinking of you all with gratitude and love."

Blair was arrested for assault and arraigned Oct. 12 on two counts of second-degree assault stemming from alleged attacks on a Port Authority police officer and a nurse following her arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles. Police had responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938.
Selma Blair broke her silence on Instagram after her arrest. (Sean Zanni)

Blair pleaded not guilty. The judge set bail at $20,000 cash, $60,000 bond or $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027.

"On Sunday, October 11, at approximately 11 p.m. at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938, which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital.
"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."

According to court documents, Blair was restrained on a stretcher at the airport but freed her leg and allegedly kicked an officer in the face, neck and chest, causing substantial swelling. A nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where Blair was taken, alleged that the actress kicked her in the chest while moving her.

Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight that departed Los Angeles earlier in the day.

"Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement. Sources told TMZ that Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another in the middle of the flight.
Law enforcement officials confirmed Blair was also separately served with a summons by the FBI and is facing one charge of assault.

title: Nicki Minaj torches Kathy Hochul as 'evil woman,' and the governor fires back with Trump jab

story: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins President Donald Trump onstage at a Michigan rally in the final stretch before the 2026 midterm elections.

Nicki Minaj is taking aim at Kathy Hochul, branding the New York governor an "evil woman" and urging voters to reject her in favor of Republican Bruce Blakeman ahead of the Nov. 3 gubernatorial election.

Minaj unleashed a series of posts on X Wednesday, accusing Hochul of failing to speak out against what the rapper described as harm to innocent people and calling on Black voters and Christians to turn against the governor.

"Kathy Hochul is an evil woman. The Democratic Party should forfeit her seat because even if she wins, she will be of great consequence to them. Downward spiral for her. She will not escape God’s wrath. She did not denounce evil when she had the chance," Minaj wrote.

The "Super Bass" singer also delivered an all-caps response to a video she reposted featuring Hochul’s controversial 2024 remark that there were "Black kids growing up in the Bronx who don’t even know what the word ‘computer’ is." Hochul apologized for the remark at the time, saying she "misspoke, and I regret it."

"How much more do you need to see & hear from them?!! How dare you as black people vote for this vile wicked curse of a woman? How dare you as Christians?! She stays silent on harm being caused to the innocent & this is what she thinks of your children! Vote Blakeman!" she posted.

Minaj also reposted a video of Hochul joking about liquor store visits while promoting her inflation rebate initiative to a predominantly Black congregation at True Bethel Baptist Church in 2025.
"Don't stop by the liquor store, OK? Buy something for the kids. Buy them some food. Sometimes I have to stop by the liquor store, too. I understand," Hochul said.
"So not only does she keep horrible company & laugh at the demonic things her friends do behind the scenes to people who aren't as politically powerful…Dear God, help us," Minaj wrote in response.
The church's bishop defended Hochul's comments at the time, saying they were made "in [the] context" of his sermon that day.

John Mellencamp isn't ready to give up the stage, even if his hearing continues to deteriorate.

The 75-year-old rock icon revealed he could be "totally deaf" by the time his upcoming tour ends, as he opened up about his worsening hearing and tinnitus during an appearance on the "Nepo, Baby!" podcast.
"I don't like going out 'cause I can't hear," Mellencamp said when asked about his hearing difficulties.
JOHN MELLENCAMP SHARES HIS UNCONVENTIONAL ADVICE TO HIS CHILDREN ABOUT WORK
John Mellencamp revealed he could be "totally deaf" by the end of his upcoming tour as he struggles with worsening hearing problems. (Timothy Norris/Getty Images for The Recording Academy)

The "Jack & Diane" singer acknowledged that years of exposure to loud rock music may have taken a toll, explaining that he experiences ringing in his ears and pulsatile tinnitus, a condition that causes him to hear his heartbeat.

"I mean, it's like right now my ears are ringing like crazy, and I have pulsatile tinnitus, which is, I hear my heartbeat. And we go into a restaurant, and it's just like, 'Well, I'm out,' because I can't hear anything because I hear all this noise and stuff. I'm sure people don't want to keep [repeating things] in my face … so just add tinnitus on top of that and it's impossible."
Pulsatile tinnitus is a rare form of tinnitus that causes people to hear sounds, such as whooshing or thumping, in time with their heartbeat, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

title: Kim Kardashian had sharp response to warnings Trump White House visit would end her career: book
summary: Kim Kardashian's White House meetings, Kanye West coparenting struggles and Kris Jenner's affair are explored in "Citizen Kim" by Jonathan Van Meter.
story: Kim Kardashian spoke at the White House about criminal justice reform and emphasized she was committed to the fight.
Kim Kardashian's life is explored in a new book chronicling her meteoric rise to fame.

In the new book, "Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future," writer Jonathan Van Meter dove deep into the lives of the Kardashians, particularly Kim, and how she built her empire outside of reality TV.

Through a series of interviews with members of the Kardashian family, including Kim, Khloe and Kourtney, as well as those close to the famous family, Van Meter discusses the biggest moments in her life, including her relationship with Kanye, the terrifying Paris robbery, her mother's affair and her prison reform and advocacy work.
A tense conversation between President Donald Trump and Kim Kardashian is just one story told in the book surrounding Kim's life. (Getty Images)
Here are some of the biggest headlines from the book.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future" is available now. (Viking)
White House warnings
Kardashian worked with Donald Trump to get clemency for a prison inmate. (Sarah Silbiger/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
In October 2017, Kim saw a video of Alice Marie Johnson in prison, in which she was pleading for clemency.
She opened up in the book about how the video "changed my life," saying she immediately reached out to Shawn Holley, who was a lawyer on O.J. Simpson's defense team, asking "What can we do?"

After learning the only way to get Johnson out of prison was a presidential pardon, Kim reached out to Ivanka Trump, who put her in touch with Jared Kushner. Kushner helped set up a meeting between Kardashian and President Trump, a move that raised concerns on both sides about the "optics," according to the book.
Kardashian was warned against meeting with President Trump in the White House, but did so anyway. (REUTERS/Bonnie Cash)

"Everyone was telling me, ‘Don’t go, your career will be over; you can’t step foot in there.’ And I was like, ‘It’s my reputation over someone’s life?’ Weigh that out," Kim said in the book. "People talk s--- about me all day long. It will just be another story about me versus someone getting their life back."
A week after the meeting with President Trump, Kim was able to call Johnson and personally deliver the news that she had been granted clemency.
A week after Kardashian's meeting with President Trump, Alice Marie Johnson was granted clemency. She later visited the White House. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

"She started screaming on the phone. I was on the set of a Steven Klein shoot, practically nude, so I had to cover with a robe and make this call and tell her," Kim said. "She packed her stuff—whatever she checked in with twenty two years prior—and was released immediately."
Oval Office meeting
Van Jones was impressed by how Kardashian was able to lead the conversation with President Trump during their meeting. (Sarah Silbiger/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Kim's experience advocating on behalf of Johnson was her first step on the path towards becoming a lawyer and furthering her advocacy work.

She met with President Trump again, this time on behalf of a man who received a life sentence for a nonviolent crime. This time, she was accompanied by attorney Van Jones, who said he will "never forget walking into the West Wing with her."

While Jones felt as if "Every sentence I said made it worse," he recalled Kim and the president discussing the case, including Kardashian's response after Trump said, "This guy . . . let's just be honest now. This is a tough guy."
Jones was impressed by how prepared and knowledgeable Kardashian was about the case during their meeting with President Trump. (Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images)

"Kim had memorized the case," Jones said in the book. "She knew everything about the person. She told the president, ‘You can be the big guy; you can help a sick man.’ It was like watching a ballerina hypnotize a grizzly bear . . . her syllable-to-impact ratio is off the charts. What she can get done in a simple sentence!"

Jones argued in the book that while some may resent Kim because "she represents somebody who already has it all" and is now trying to also "be successful in my field," he says, "if you’re in jail, and you’re trying to get out, you’re not mad at Kim Kardashian."
KIM KARDASHIAN WOWS IN STRING BIKINI DURING PDA-FILLED BEACH TRIP WITH LEWIS HAMILTON
Jones said people are mad at Kardashian because she is already successful, but said they should be more upset at the system. (Katie Jones/Variety/Penske Media via Getty Images)

"You have literally hundreds of thousands of people for whom the system is so broken that only when a Kim Kardashian steps in does she change the odds in their favor, even a little bit," he said. "So you can be mad at Kim or you can be mad at the system that is so broken that it needs Kim."
Kanye concerns
Kardashian and West tied the knot in May 2014. (Jon Kopaloff/FilmMagic)
Kim married rapper Kanye West in May 2014 and welcomed four children together before filing for divorce in February 2021.

Towards the end of their marriage, West began acting increasingly erratic as he dealt with ongoing mental health issues and began speaking negatively about Kim and her family members. Kim expressed in the past that this led her to not feel safe around him, emotionally and physically.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
The two welcomed four children together before splitting in 2021. (James Devaney/GC Images)
Despite this, Kim told Van Meter she continues to "worry about him all day."

"All the time. That’s the father of my kids, I’ll never not worry about him. And that’s a big burden of having kids with someone who you don’t necessarily get along with. My kids would never know that. I do everything in my power to forget about all the negative things that happened," she said. "I have to be realistic, and my therapist definitely tells me, ‘Your boundaries have to go up,’ but we manage to coparent without too much conflict. It’s been pretty smooth for while. I guess because we don’t talk that much. But when we see each other, we give each other a hug."

She added that she not only encourages her children to have a relationship with their father, but also with his family, noting that whenever his family members are in town, she will invite them over for dinner and to spend time with her kids.
While the two are divorced, Kardashian says she worries about him all the time and encourages her children to have a relationship with him and his family. (Pierre Suu/Getty Images)
Although he was acting erratic in public, Kim noted their children never saw him that way, adding, "That was such a blessing."

"He would have a full episode, and the kids would never know because they would be almost a calming presence for him. So it was a fine balance of, like, how do we keep them around? Or: Is it go-time?" she said. "My whole household knows what a ‘lockdown’ means if I text it. Like, ‘We’re on lockdown.’ No TVs, just movies. No just plug in a phone for music in the car. Not even, like, XM, because they talk about current events in real time. like, they don’t have to be a party to this."

A house divided
Jenner was married to Robert Kardashian Sr. until 1990, when she was caught having an affair. (Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images)
Kris Jenner's marriage to Robert Kardashian ended in 1990 when she was caught having an affair with 23-year-old soccer player, Todd Waterman.

In her own memoir, Jenner opened up about the affair, calling it "out of control, crazy, dangerous." Van Meter writes that as time went on she got "reckless" and would openly host friends at her home along with Waterman, and even took six-year-old Khloe with her when she went on dates with him.

"We knew my mom was dating, because we would see it," Kim said. "She introduced us to her boyfriend. He was ten years younger. He was kind of like a playboy."
Kardashian said she knew her mom was dating because he brought him around them. (Jonny Marlow/Disney via Getty Images)
Robert eventually confronted Jenner, and they came together to tell their children they were getting a divorce in January 1990.

When reflecting on that day, Kim shared that "Kourtney had a hard time with it" and that "I didn't really care." Kourtney confirmed this saying, "I don't think it affected her," when asked about Kim's reaction.
The book confirmed Kourtney Kardashian took their parent's separation the hardest. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for Boohoo)
"It was traumatic for me," Kourtney told Van Meter. "I feel like the oldest child takes things the hardest. I see that with my own kids and my nieces and nephews."
OJ's opinion
O.J. Simpson reportedly said "Keeping Up with the Kardashians" wouldn't last on air for more than two weeks. (Steve Marcus-Pool/Getty Images)
When "Keeping Up with the Kardashians" aired its first episode in October 2007, audiences gained access to the Kardashian/Jenner clan in a way they previously never had.
Prior to the release of the show, Kim appeared on "The Tyra Banks Show" in September, and after seeing her on the show, O.J. Simpson wasn't too hopeful the show would be a success.

While in Las Vegas getting ready to commit armed robbery to allegedly steal sports memorabilia he believed to be his, memorabilia dealer, Tom Riccio, who was in the room with him, recalled the former football star saying, "That’s my goddaughter! Her name is Kim!" and then added, "That show ain’t gonna last two weeks!"
"Keeping Up with the Kardashians" ended up being a massive success with many spin-offs. (Medios y Media/Getty Images)

Of course, the show ultimately went on to air on E! for over 14 years and spawned eight spin-off shows. Their reality TV prowess continues on Hulu, as their new show, "The Kardashians" recently started its eighth season on the streamer.

title: 'Days of our Lives' star Robert Kelker-Kelly's cause of death revealed
summary: Robert Kelker-Kelly complained of chest and left arm pain after landing at Spirit of St. Louis Airport before his death from heart disease at 62.
story: The 'Days of Our Lives' actor experienced alarming symptoms before his wife found him unresponsive, a police report reveals. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)
Robert Kelker-Kelly, the actor best known for playing Bo Brady on "Days of Our Lives," died from arteriosclerotic heart disease, the St. Charles County medical examiner confirmed to Fox News Digital.
The medical examiner ruled his death natural.

Kelker-Kelly, who also worked as a professional pilot, experienced chest and left arm pain shortly before his death at age 62, according to a St. Peters Police Department report obtained by Fox News Digital.
'DAYS OF OUR LIVES' STAR ROBERT KELKER-KELLY IGNORED ALARMING SYMPTOMS BEFORE SUDDEN DEATH: POLICE REPORT
Robert Kelker-Kelly as Bo Brady on set during a wedding scene.  (Gary Null / NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Images)

His wife, Allison Kelly, told police she picked up her husband from Spirit of St. Louis Airport at approximately 7:30 p.m. Oct. 3. During the drive home, Kelker-Kelly complained of pain in his chest and left arm and asked her to pull over so he could vomit, the report stated.
Kelly asked her husband whether he needed to go to the hospital. He declined, instead asking her to take him home so he could lie down.
After arriving at their Missouri residence, Kelker-Kelly changed his clothes and got into bed. He continued experiencing pain and asked his wife to get him an aspirin, according to the report.
When Kelly returned from the kitchen, she found her husband unresponsive and not breathing.
HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S FINAL MOMENTS REVEALED IN FRANTIC 911 CALL FROM BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER
Robert Kelker-Kelly has died at 62. (Paul Drinkwater / NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Images)
She immediately called 911 and began performing CPR, the report stated.
St. Peters police and the St. Charles County Ambulance District responded to the home shortly after 8 p.m.. Paramedics attempted lifesaving measures, but Kelker-Kelly was pronounced dead at 9:09 p.m.

According to the report, Kelly told investigators her husband had no known medical conditions and was not taking prescription medications. She also said he had not had any serious injuries or had surgery during the previous year.
‘SAVED BY THE BELL’ STAR DENNIS HASKINS DEAD AT 75
Robert Kelker-Kelly and Lisa Rinna pose as their characters from "Days of Our Lives." (Joseph Del Valle / NBCU Photo Bank)
Police told Fox News Digital at the time that investigators found no suspicious circumstances at the scene.
"Mr. Kelly had reportedly complained of chest pain shortly before becoming unresponsive, and the circumstances appeared consistent with a medical event," police said.
The St. Charles County Medical Examiner's office released Kelker-Kelly without requesting further investigation, according to the report.

title: Russell Brand’s wife defends actor at rape trial while admitting his past monogamy struggles
summary: Laura Brand opened up about Russell Brand's difficulty with monogamy and their love story amid his ongoing rape and sexual assault trial in court. He has denied all charges.
story: Allegations of rape and sexual assault lead to the trial of Russell Brand in London. Prosecutors describe Brand as a 'ruthless sexual predator' as the case involving six women opens. Brand denies the charges and states he is hopeful for a good outcome. Fox News correspondent Stephanie Bennett reports on the expected six-week trial.
Russell Brand’s wife, Laura Brand, took the stand Thursday as a defense witness, one day after the comedian and actor testified in his ongoing rape and sexual assault trial.

Brand, 51, is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges and vehemently denies the allegations.

According to Sky News, Brand acknowledged that he had been "reckless" and used his fame to pursue sexual relationships, but insisted that the encounters were consensual. He also told the jury that consent was "fundamental, essential and necessary."
RUSSELL BRAND ACCUSED OF RAPE, SEXUAL ABUSE OF 4 WOMEN; COMEDIAN DENIES ‘SERIOUS CRIMINAL ALLEGATIONS’
Russell Brand's wife, Laura Brand, took the stand in the actor's rape and sexual assault trial. (Getty Images)
During Laura's testimony, the mom of three — who first met her husband when she was 19, and he was 31 — opened up about the start of their relationship.
The pair began dating in 2006, but split the following year due to Brand’s difficulty with monogamy and her "inexperience."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"When I met him, I was aware that he liked women, and I was aware toward the latter half of that year that he was engaging with other women," Laura told the court, per Sky News. "I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people. I was invested; we both had told each other we loved each other, but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous."
The allegations against Russell Brand were first brought to light in 2023. (Mike Marsland/WireImage)
The couple rekindled their relationship in 2015 and married in 2017. They share three children.
Laura described Brand as "caring and kind, a wonderful father to our children, and an amazing, attentive husband," adding that he has an "eye for detail I have never known before."

"I feel very seen by him," she said. "We have a very honest, frank and clear relationship and marriage.… Our relationship has always been [about] honesty. I love him very much."
According to the outlet, there was a brief moment of tension in court when defense attorney Ian Winter asked Laura about her "view as to the truth of the allegations."
The judge quickly intervened, telling the attorney that Laura was not an expert witness. The jury was temporarily sent out of the courtroom.
Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London on Oct. 29, 2026, ahead of his trial on rape and sexual assault charges. He has denied all charges. (Getty Images)
HARVEY WEINSTEIN SENTENCED TO 15 YEARS IN PRISON FOR 2006 SEX CRIME IN NEW YORK

Prosecutors allege that Brand committed the offenses against six women over a 10-year period. The women have testified in court about alleged encounters at a hotel, a bar, a radio station, a workplace and Brand’s home.
Brand has denied forcing any of the women to engage in sexual activity against their will.
KATY PERRY FIGHTS BACK AGAINST RUBY ROSE'S 'CATEGORICALLY FALSE' SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS
In a video posted to X last year, Brand thanked his fans for messages of support, then criticized the British government and legal system before addressing the charges directly.

He explained that he "was a fool before I lived in the light of the Lord. I was a drug addict, a sex addict and an imbecile, but what I never was was a rapist. I've never engaged in nonconsensual activity. I pray that you can see that by looking in my eyes."
Brand added, "Of course, I'm now going to have the opportunity to defend these charges in court, and I'm incredibly grateful for that."
He wrapped up his video by assuring his followers that he'd continue to address the allegations against him.
As police explained in a press release, detectives began investigating Brand after allegations were made public by U.K. media outlets Channel 4 and The Sunday Times in September 2023.

The outlets launched a joint investigation into the allegations, resulting in a lengthy article on the Times' website, as well as an episode of Channel 4's documentary series, "Dispatches," called "Russell Brand: In Plain Sight." Both contained a number of anonymous complaints, with women accusing Brand of physical and emotional abuse and bullying, as well as some instances of sexual assault.

title: Patrick Stewart, legendary 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' actor, dies at 86
summary: Legendary "Star Trek" and "X-Men" actor Patrick Stewart died at his Los Angeles home at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
story: The Associated Press revisits memorable moments from Patrick Stewart's decades-long career on stage and screen, including his celebrated portrayals of Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Professor Charles Xavier, following his death at 86.

Sir Patrick Stewart, the legendary British actor best known for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek" and Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" franchise, has died at 86, according to a statement shared on his Instagram account.

Stewart died Wednesday at his Los Angeles home, surrounded by family and friends and cared for by his wife, Sunny, following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, the statement said.

"We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," Stewart's longtime spokeswoman Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."She added that he went from his home in Yorkshire to the Royal Shakespeare Company and on to an "equally acclaimed career spanning six decades on Broadway, the silver screen and television."
PATRICK STEWART: A LIFE IN PICTURES

Legendary "Star Trek" and "X-Men" actor, Patrick Stewart, died on October 28 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. He was 86. (Photo by Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures)
Actor Patrick Stewart, Captain Picard of Star Trek: The Next Generation, poses for a portrait circa 1987 in Los Angeles, California  (Aaron Rapoport/Corbis/Getty Images)

"His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre," she wrote. "He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise."

HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOSBush Novak said that Stewart's professional accomplishments were "humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans’ mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster pitties. He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan. He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life."
‘STAR TREK’ STAR PATRICK STEWART RECALLS VIOLENT CHILDHOOD WITH BRITISH ARMY FATHER
While Stewart was best known for his TV and film sci-fi roles, he was a prolific — and classically trained theater actor.
Stewart was first discovered for the part of Jean-Luc Picard by a "Star Trek: The Next Generation" producer when he was reading Shakespeare at a UCLA lecture.
PATRICK STEWART CONFIRMS 'STAR TREK' RETURN AS JEAN-LUC PICARD
Patrick Stewart as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation." (CBS via Getty Images)
The actor didn't expect the series, which revamped the original "Star Trek" starring William Shatner, to go past one season.

"I was very naïve about the conditions attached to series television in the U.S.A.," Stewart admitted to Startrek.com in 2010, explaining he found out he had to sign a six-year contract for the series. "Every single person I spoke to – agents, directors, screenwriters, other actors – said, ‘Oh, don’t worry about six years. You’ll be lucky to make it through the first year.’ Everybody felt it was madness to try to revive an iconic series like William Shatner and Leonard Nimoy’s Star Trek. So, on the basis of that advice I signed the six-year contract."
The series ended up running for seven seasons and spawned four films: "Star Trek: Generations," "Star Trek: First Contact," "Star Trek: Insurrection," and "Star Trek: Nemesis."
Shatner paid tribute to Stewart on Thursday afternoon.

"What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner wrote. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed."

His "X-Men co-star Hugh Jackman wrote on X: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

"Star Trek" star George Takei wrote on X that fans "across the world" were mourning the loss of a "true and irreplaceable legend. As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before. He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Despite becoming one of the most iconic faces of the "Star Trek" universe and taking on the part of Professor Charles Xavier in nine films, starting with "X-Men" in 2000, Stewart largely avoided becoming typecast as he said he feared.
Patrick Stewart pictured in 1999's "A Christmas Carol." (Oliver Upton /© TNT / Courtesy Everett Collection)

He was cast in 1991's "L.A. Story," "Robin Hood: Men in Tights," "Conspiracy Theory," the TV miniseries "Moby Dick," "A Christmas Carol," "A Lion in Winter," "Extras," a 2009 TV movie of "Hamlet" in which he played Claudius, and Seth MacFarlane comedies "Blunt Talk" and "American Dad."
Stewart even voiced one of the sheep in Amazon's "The Sheep Detectives," which came out earlier this year.
He most recently reprised his "Star Trek" role in 2020 for a three-season run on "Star Trek: Picard" for Paramount+.

MacFarlane paid tribute to Stewart on his Instagram on Thursday, writing that he "grew up as a fan, and was later gifted the privilege of becoming a colleague and friend, working with him for many years on ‘American Dad!’, ‘Family Guy’, and ‘Ted’. He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come. I remember exchanging emails with him a number of years ago when he was beginning day 1 of a new film. He commented to me that he always walked onto a new set feeling like the biggest novice there. My stunned reaction was the same as anyone’s would be. I said, ‘Patrick, if you feel that way, the rest of us are screwed.’ We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
He received Emmy nominations for "Moby Dick," "A Lion in Winter," "Extras," and "Hamlet."
Sir Patrick Stewart wearing a tuxedo while attending the BAFTA Film Awards in 2023. (Carlo Paloni/BAFTA via Getty Images)
On stage, Stewart played Claudius, Ebenezer Scrooge and received his only Tony nomination for his starring role in "Macbeth" on Broadway, following a run in London's West End.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Nearly 50 years I’ve waited," Stewart told The Associated Press in 2008. "I learned it when I was 14. I memorized all the soliloquies just because I thought they were great. And they stuck, so I didn’t have to learn those bits of the play, which is a blessing, because learning lines has now become the one curse of this job."
Stewart married his third wife, Sunny Ozell, in 2013. He is also survived by two children, a daughter, Sophia, and a son, Daniel.

story: The "Ransom Canyon" star recently sold one of his Los Angeles homes, choosing instead to invest his money in his new homebase, Fargo, North Dakota.
Josh Duhamel is encouraging Minnesotans to get out and vote in a new video he shared on Instagram.
The actor took to social media to send out a "PSA to the great people of Minnesota," rallying residents to pack the polls in what he dubbed "God's country."

"I just wanted to take a second to remind you that the midterms are coming up. This is such an important, such an important time. We have to get out there. We have to vote. Every single person," he said. "Minnesota is my second favorite state in the whole country, right behind North Dakota, but I absolutely love it there. It is God's country. It is worth saving. It is absolutely worth saving."
While he said he "would never tell you who to vote for," he believes voting is one's "job as an American citizen" and a "sacred duty."

In the caption, Duhamel encouraged his followers to "Bring a group to the voting booths on Nov 3" and to share the post "with everyone you know!!"
Although the actor didn't endorse any candidates, people in the comments section made their own assumptions as to what he meant when he said the state is "worth saving."
"Worth saving means vote red. Good man @joshduhamel," one fan wrote in the comments section. "Red red red all down the ballot," another added, while a third wrote, "Vote RED! Save America."

title: 'Lioness' star Jill Wagner raises daughters in Tennessee town of 800, where horses and buggies still roam
summary: "A Very Arctic Christmas" and "Lioness" star Jill Wagner traded Hollywood for a Tennessee town of 800, where Mennonites ride horses and buggies.
story: "A Very Arctic Christmas" star tells Fox News Digital why she traded Hollywood's fast pace for small-town Tennessee and the life lessons she hopes her daughters will carry into adulthood.
From the high-stakes action of "Lioness" to the holiday adventure of "A Very Arctic Christmas," Jill Wagner is taking on two very different worlds.

But off camera, the actress has traded Hollywood's hustle for a quieter life raising her two daughters on a Tennessee farm in a town of just 800 people — where horses and buggies are still a familiar sight.
"First of all, I love Tennessee … I'm from the South. I'm from North Carolina," she told Fox News Digital. "I love the people here but especially love the small-town mentality."
'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME
Life in her Tennessee town offers a glimpse of a world that can feel far removed from Hollywood.
Jill Wagner reunites with Cameron Mathison in "A Very Arctic Christmas," bringing her signature holiday charm. (Great American Media)
"I was at the post office this morning and one of the Mennonites was in front of me … I got to look at their horse and buggy," she said.
Wagner said the small-town atmosphere has become an important part of the childhood she and her husband want to give their girls.
The actress explained why she hopes her daughters will eventually appreciate the slower pace, even if they someday follow in her footsteps and move to bigger cities.
WATCH: JILL WAGNER TRADES HOLLYWOOD HUSTLE FOR TENNESSEE FAMILY LIFE
"In some ways, going back to a simpler, slower pace … I think as we get older, or at least I know I can speak for myself, as I get older, I really value that," she added.
Wagner knows the pull of Hollywood firsthand. She left home at 17 to pursue a career in entertainment and suspects her daughters may one day be eager to spread their own wings.
But she hopes they'll always remember what their upbringing gave them.
‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’

"And I'm sure they'll do the same, but I hope what it does is bring them back to the simple-ness of life and what it can be … That's a gift that my husband and I gave them, and they probably don't even know it yet," she said.
Jill Wagner and Cameron Mathison stand together at a wildlife rehabilitation facility decorated for Christmas for the film, "A Very Arctic Christmas." (Great American Media)
Away from the action of "Lioness," Wagner is embracing the holiday spirit in "A Very Arctic Christmas," reuniting with Cameron Mathison for a festive adventure.
Wagner plays Jane, a wildlife conservationist who helps a father and daughter navigate an unexpected Arctic adventure after their holiday cruise goes off course.
"Lioness" star Jill Wagner says raising her daughters with small-town values is a gift they may not fully appreciate until they're older. (Lauren Smith/Paramount+)
The actress said working with Mathison brings plenty of laughs to "A Very Arctic Christmas" set.

"There's never any dull moment when you have Cameron Mathison and I on set together. In fact, it's hard for us to get through a scene without laughing, I'm sure. Robin Dunne, the director, is always rolling his eyes, like, ‘Oh, guys, guys, guys, guys, bring it in,'" she laughed.
WATCH: JILL WAGNER DISHES ON THE ON-SET CHAOS WITH CO-STAR CAMERON MATHISON
For Wagner, the holiday films also have a personal connection.
The actress has found ways to include her daughters in her Christmas-movie tradition.
When Wagner's daughters were younger, she included them in one of her films as extras, giving them a chance to sit on Santa's lap.
Now that they're older, Wagner said they understand that Christmas movies are a genre of their own — and she hopes the experience becomes a lasting family tradition.

"And I just hope that one day when I'm long and gone, that is a tradition with each other's families is that they get on Christmas, and they get to watch that movie and just kind of laugh at the fact that we're all in a movie together at Christmas," she added.

While Wagner's career continues to take her between intense action roles and feel-good holiday projects, she values sharing those experiences with her daughters while giving them a childhood rooted in small-town life.
Jill Wagner and husband David Lemanowicz kissing at the "Lioness" Season 2 premiere. (Variety via Getty Images)
When Fox News Digital asked whether her daughters were becoming the Tennessee farm girls she had envisioned, Wagner admitted there's still some work to do.
"So, I don't know about farm girl. I know that … they love outdoors. They don't necessarily like doing farm work. So, we're trying to still work on that," she laughed.
"They do love running around barefooted in the dirt, and they can play outside all day long, which I love for them," Wagner said.
The family hopes to add chickens and goats when Wagner's work schedule allows more time at home.
"Maybe one day we'll get a horse or a pony for them," she added.

Her family owns Scott Mansion Farms, where they host charitable events benefiting the Special Operations Warrior Foundation and Dolly Parton's Children's Hospital. Wagner said the community's support has been especially meaningful.

title: Collin Gosselin calls out reality TV producers for putting ratings ahead of kids: 'The show must go on'
summary: Collin Gosselin's memoir alleges child exploitation on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," claiming production priorities came at the expense of his well-being.
story: The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star tells Fox News Digital reality TV puts children at risk when adults ignore their discomfort.
Collin Gosselin is sounding the alarm on the reality TV industry, accusing adults of turning a blind eye when children are hurting — all to keep the cameras rolling.

The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star is revisiting the painful realities of his youth in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood," alleging that what made for compelling television often came at the expense of the children living it.
"It's the simple fact that adults that are seeing these things, they surely understood that people are choosing not to say anything because the show must go on," Collin told Fox News Digital.
'JON & KATE PLUS 8' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN ACCUSES MOM OF TRYING TO 'BURY' HIM TO 'PROTECT HER REPUTATION'
Kate continued filming with her children following her split from Jon Gosselin. (Donna Svennevik/Disney General Entertainment Content)
"And if, at any point in time, a child can voice that they do not want to film, we need to take that seriously," he said.

Collin, one of the sextuplets who rose to fame alongside his parents and siblings, said children should not have to clearly articulate their distress before the adults around them recognize something is wrong.

"To understand and to know that at a young age, at any age, means that you really, you feel in your heart that it is not right, and you know you're being exploited and that's crazy for a child to know," he said. "But we should listen to that because that's a huge thing."
WATCH HERE: COLLIN GOSSELIN CALLS OUT REALITY TV PRODUCERS FOR PUTTING RATINGS AHEAD OF KIDS

Collin Gosselin says growing up in front of reality TV cameras came at an emotional cost, alleging that warning signs were ignored to keep filming. (Donna Svennevik/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images, Brad Barket/WireImage for Discovery Communications)
Even when children remain silent, Collin argued, adults have a responsibility to pay attention.

"But even without a child saying anything, you can tell, you can absolutely tell. It's reading body language," Collin said. "You can absolutely tell and we should be aware. We should be paying attention. We should be protecting children."
WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN BLASTS MOM KATE FOR 'BURYING' HIM TO SAVE HER REPUTATION
Collin said the show's production priorities came at the expense of his well-being and that of his siblings, arguing that the demands of filming conflicted with what was best for the children.

"100% my entire childhood, what was best for production was this direct relationship to what was unhealthy for a child," he said. "But nobody cared about the welfare of me and my siblings, they cared about my paycheck."
He also said his siblings were kept in the dark about what happened at home while they were at school, adding that he hopes they will examine his account for themselves.
JON GOSSELIN CLAIMS HE'S 'PERFECT STRANGERS NOW' WITH SIX OF HIS KIDS AFTER YEARS OF NO CONTACT
"A lot happened that was kept from them intentionally so that they could be told that their brother was this and that," Collin said.
As filming intensified, Collin said the family's public image took priority over the children's experiences at home.
Left to right are sextuplet twins Aaden J Gosselin, Leah H Gosselin, Collin T Gosselin, Joel K Gosselin, Alexis F Gosselin and Hannah J Gosselin. (MediaNews Group/Reading Eagle via Getty Images)

"But once everything got going, and we were at the height of filming and production, it was absolutely more about what it looked like on the outside and not necessarily how me and my siblings felt," he said. "It was always about how it looked for everybody else."
For Collin, the failure is not simply recognizing that something is wrong, but refusing to act.
"Doing something about it because the biggest thing is when we know something's wrong, and we don't say anything that's worse than not knowing it," he said.
Collin said the family that audiences watched on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" did not reflect the full reality of his childhood, arguing that viewers saw a more polished version of life at home.
KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR
When asked what cameras failed to capture, he described experiences and opportunities that he said were offered to the children for filming but later taken away.

His criticism goes beyond editing and production decisions. Collin also revisited his experience of being placed in a treatment facility and given medication, describing a period when he felt stripped of control over his life.

"For a long time, my name was dragged, and I was put away. I was essentially put in a juvenile prison, put on all these medications," he said. "I was a zombie half the time. I had no control, I had nothing."
WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN DETAILS ALLEGED ABUSE, CONFRONTS FAMILY TRAUMA
He said he spent that time doing what he was told, with little ability to change his circumstances.
"I did what I was told. I went through the motions, and was like a zombie every day," he said.
Reflecting on that experience, Collin said he feels compelled to speak publicly about what happened.
"And so when you reflect on all that, you realize these things need to be talked about, and I feel just an urge to talk about them," he said.

Collin said he has not spoken to his mother. He recalled a visit from Kate when he was 13, claiming the encounter left him with a painful final memory.
"She berated me for all of 20 minutes after not seeing me for over a year," he said.
Meanwhile, Collin told Fox News Digital he held on to hope even during what he described as his darkest moments.
Collin Gosselin is speaking out about his childhood on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," accusing adults behind the scenes of prioritizing production over children's well-being. (Getty Images)
"I had very little hope, but I always had some, and I hung on to that … I just kept telling myself that there's a better future for me and there will be a time where I will be past this," he said.
The former child star said sharing his story had weighed on him for years before he finally decided to speak publicly.
"It was heavy on my heart to tell my story and to hope that it would create change," he said.
As for reconciliation with his mother, Collin said an apology alone would not be enough to repair their relationship.

Collin opened up about his alleged abuse in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight." (Michael Simon/Getty Images)

"Reconciliation requires action and accountability," he said. "I think we can all say, I'm sorry, but if we're not willing to take the actions and take accountability for what has happened in the past and what happened my entire childhood, then what does that really mean, you know?"
"Jon & Kate Plus 8" followed Jon and Kate Gosselin as they raised their twin daughters, Mady and Cara, alongside their sextuplets: Collin, Alexis, Hannah, Aaden, Leah and Joel.

title: Macklemore called 'out of touch' over speech at Free Palestine Tour kickoff
summary: Macklemore launched his Free Palestine Tour in Dublin with defiant remarks about his removal from Ed Sheeran's lineup, sparking mixed reactions.
story: Former Israeli special envoy Noa Tishby discusses rising antisemitism in America, the fallout from the Macklemore-Ed Sheeran controversy and more on ‘My View with Lara Trump.’
Macklemore took his political message to a new stage.
The rapper doubled down on his pro-Palestinian activism during the launch of his Free Palestine Tour, weeks after his controversial remarks prompted his removal from Ed Sheeran's lineup.

"I ​am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will ​continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath," Macklemore told the crowd during his concert in Dublin, according to Reuters.
"Six weeks ago, two words is all ​that it took," he said, referring to the fallout after he declared "Free Palestine" while opening for Ed Sheeran.

Macklemore doubled down on his "Free Palestine" remarks during the opening of his tour. (Zoe Rain/Reuters)

"Those two words are so threatening to some people that we'd rather silence those two words than confront what they ​actually mean. ... Somehow those words have become more controversial than the suffering that made them necessary," Macklemore added.

Macklemore's defiant remarks drew mixed reactions online, with some social media users applauding his outspoken activism while others questioned his motives and accused him of being out of touch. Critics also took aim at the rapper's priorities, suggesting he should focus his attention on problems closer to home rather than delivering political speeches onstage.

GIGI HADID SAYS HER RELATIONSHIP WITH BRADLEY COOPER PROVIDES SOMETHING SHE HASN'T EXPERIENCED BEFORE

"Yes, there is a huge age gap there, OK?" Chrisley, 29, said of Jason during the podcast. "And that’s probably part of the reason why I kept a lot of it quiet, because I know how brutal the public can be. But I genuinely do not care.
Savannah Chrisley announced she is engaged and expecting her first baby with her partner, Jason.  (Getty Images)

"I have always said, ‘I would rather [have] 20 phenomenal, unbelievable years with someone than 50 ‘meh’ years.' Like, the amount of love and respect that we have, we have so many dreams, and we dream together, we work together … we want to have life experiences with each other. title: E. coli outbreak lands 3 in hospital, health officials investigate link to pumpkin patch
summary: Three children are in intensive care after an E. coli outbreak potentially linked to Brookshire Farms pumpkin patch in San Luis Obispo, California.
story: Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious disease physician and founder of Wellness Equity Alliance in California, speaks with Fox News Digital about E. coli infections linked to a California pumpkin patch that closed just days before Halloween.
Three children are in intensive care with E. coli infections as health officials investigate a possible link to a California pumpkin patch that closed just days before Halloween.

Five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection have been confirmed, potentially originating from Brookshire Farms in San Luis Obispo, according to an Oct. 27 advisory issued by the County of San Luis Obispo Public Health Department.
The suspected exposure period is Oct. 16 through Oct 26.
FDA WIDENS CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK INVESTIGATION TO SIX MORE STATES AS CONFIRMED CASES TOP 6,000
Health officials advise that anyone who visited the pumpkin patch between those dates should monitor for gastrointestinal symptoms.
Three children are in intensive care with E. coli infections as health officials investigate a possible link to a California pumpkin patch that closed just days before Halloween. (Getty Images)
"We are working diligently to identify the source of these infections to protect the health of our community," said County Health Officer Dr. Christy Mulkerin in the news release.
"We encourage anyone who may have been exposed and is experiencing symptoms consistent with E. coli infection to seek immediate medical attention."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Typical symptoms of E. coli include cramping, severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and signs of dehydration, which usually begin within three to 10 days of exposure.

Young children under 10 are typically at the highest risk for complications, which can include hemolytic uremic syndrome, a serious condition that damages blood cells and can lead to kidney failure, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
"We are working diligently to identify the source of these infections to protect the health of our community," said County Health Officer Dr. Christy Mulkerin in the news release. (iStock)
Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious disease physician and founder of Wellness Equity Alliance in California, warned that diarrhea can lead to dehydration and fatigue.
"The diarrhea is really the key component here, and the stomach cramps," he told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Evans said younger children and older adults can be particularly vulnerable, emphasizing the need to closely watch children younger than 5.
Typical symptoms of E. coli include cramping, severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and signs of dehydration, which usually begin within three to 10 days of exposure. (iStock)
Speaking generally about potential exposure routes in pumpkin patches, Evans said E. coli can spread when bacteria from feces reach someone’s mouth.
He pointed to potentially contaminated food or water, animal contact and person-to-person transmission as possible transmission routes.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Evans also noted that not all E. coli bacteria cause illness. The confirmed cases in this investigation involve Shiga toxin-producing E. coli.
"One of the most effective ways that we can prevent this is washing your hands," the doctor added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The farm has voluntarily closed as a precaution while investigators work to identify the source of the infections, determine whether the cases are connected and assess whether others may be at risk, according to the county health department.
Brookshire Farms told Fox News Digital it was reserving comment pending test results from the county health department.

title: Common developmental condition linked to higher risk of Parkinson's-related disorders
summary: Older adults with autism were diagnosed with parkinsonism at more than double the rate of the general population, a study of 57 million Americans found.
story: Dr. Chadrick Lane, a neuropsychiatrist and director of the geriatric and neuropsychiatry clinic at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas, Texas, said humor can be a helpful wellness tool for those navigating the Parkinson's journey.

Older adults diagnosed with autism face a significantly higher risk of developing Parkinson’s disease-related movement disorders compared to the general population, according to a large new study published in the journal Autism.
Researchers analyzed Medicare and Medicaid claims data covering nearly 57 million Americans aged 45 and older between 2017 and 2019.
Individuals on the spectrum, as well as those with intellectual disabilities, were diagnosed with parkinsonism at much higher rates than those without autism.
HOW EATING HABITS COULD INFLUENCE PARKINSON’S DISEASE RISK, ACCORDING TO EXPERTS

Parkinsonism refers to a range of neurological conditions characterized by certain movement symptoms, including tremors, muscle rigidity, balance difficulties and slowed voluntary movement, according to the Parkinson’s Foundation.

While earlier research suggested an overlap between autism and motor decline later in life, it was unclear whether those problems stemmed from the condition or from antipsychotic medications, which are widely known to trigger Parkinson’s-like symptoms as a secondary side effect.

A nationwide study of nearly 57 million Americans aged 45 and older revealed that adults with autism and intellectual disabilities are diagnosed with Parkinson’s-related movement disorders at rates far exceeding those in the general population. (iStock)

To determine whether medications explained the link, researchers excluded people who took antipsychotics from the analysis. They still found higher rates of Parkinson’s-related diagnoses in neurodivergent populations.

In the general population control group, the prevalence of parkinsonism was roughly 1.57%. The prevalence rose to 3.83% among adults with autism alone, 4.32% for those with an intellectual disability alone, and 4.86% among individuals diagnosed with both autism and an intellectual disability.
PARKINSON’S PATIENT’S YEARS-LONG TREMOR VANISHES WITHIN MINUTES OF NEW ULTRASOUND TREATMENT

"A critically important new contribution of this study is increased incidence rates of parkinsonism for autistic people in middle and older adulthood, which suggests that these cases aren’t simply a byproduct of lifelong motor challenges," Greg Wallace, lead author and a professor in the Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences at The George Washington University in Washington, D.C., said in a press release.
The study represents the first time scientists have tracked the incidence rate, or the risk of newly emerging cases over time, among older autistic individuals.
The risk of parkinsonism persisted even after researchers completely eliminated individuals taking antipsychotic medications, ruling out common drug-induced side effects as the sole driver. (iStock)
"It is therefore important for clinicians to establish clear baselines of motor skills and challenges during adulthood that can be tracked over time," Wallace added.
Dr. Lee Murray, a neurologist based in Jackson, Tennessee, said this study clarifies previous research that suggested patients with autism are at a higher risk of having Parkinson's.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This study takes into account the use of antipsychotic medications that can cause a Parkinson's look (resting tremor, stiffness, shuffled gait, stooped posture, softened voice), which is a different pathology than stereotypical or idiopathic Parkinson's disease," Murray, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital.
"This study showed patients with autism that was associated with intellectual disability seem to have the greatest association with concomitant Parkinson's."

The neurologist cautioned that autism encompasses a wide range of symptoms and severity, so the findings don't mean that people with milder cases face a significantly higher risk of Parkinson’s disease.
"It certainly is an interesting correlation, although it does not imply that someone with autism is certain to develop Parkinson's," Murray added.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
"From a clinical perspective, it's helpful to review medications with the autistic patient's physicians and, if possible, try to avoid medications that may cause a Parkinson's appearance."
Despite the scope of the data, the authors noted several key limitations of using insurance records.
A major limitation of the research stems from its reliance on Medicare and Medicaid billing records, which carry risks of diagnostic coding errors. (iStock)

The investigation relied on billing and diagnostic codes submitted through Medicare and Medicaid, which can contain errors or reflect differences in how clinics and medical providers diagnose conditions.
The reliance on claims data also means researchers could not assess the severity of individual motor symptoms or examine the role of lifestyle factors, genetics and family history, they noted.

Additionally, the data only captured adults who were enrolled in public insurance programs, potentially leaving out older individuals who rely strictly on private health insurance.
"Patients with autism can have atypical movements that can be misdiagnosed as Parkinson's if the examiner is not accustomed to diagnosing it."

Because people on the autism spectrum may already struggle with coordination, repetitive behaviors or executive functioning challenges, experts say early indicators of Parkinson’s disease can be missed or mistaken, potentially delaying essential care.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Patients with autism can have atypical movements that can be misdiagnosed as Parkinson's if the examiner is not accustomed to diagnosing it," Murray confirmed.

The researchers emphasized the need for physicians, long-term care facilities and family caregivers to closely monitor older autistic patients for motor decline so interventions can begin as early as possible.
