He said it was possible that there were hundreds of Afghans at the Central Louisiana ICE Processing Center, which has served as a hub for ICE detainees before their deportation from the U.S.

If the U.S. sends Afghan detainees to Pakistan, they are not likely to be there long. Pakistan, which has hosted millions of Afghan refugees for decades, launched a sweeping crackdown in 2023, pressuring hundreds of thousands of Afghans to leave the country and forcibly deporting others.

They are arriving to an Afghanistan battered by multiple humanitarian crises, including widespread malnutrition, as well as an ongoing military conflict with neighboring Pakistan and a dramatic rollback of women’s rights under the Taliban’s hard-line Islamic policies.
VanDiver said the Trump administration would most likely be aware that Afghans sent to Pakistan would be at high risk of being returned to Afghanistan.
“You don’t have to be that smart to figure out that they’re sending them to Pakistan so that Pakistan will finish the job,” he said.

Regardless of whether they worked with the U.S. military, VanDiver said, any Afghans flown from the U.S. would be viewed with suspicion by the Taliban and at risk of persecution, imprisonment or worse.
That does not appear to be a major concern for the White House, said the senior administration official, who declined to be identified because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
“The administration’s position is, ‘These individuals do not have status in our country, therefore we don’t really care what happens to them,’” the official said.

VanDiver and others say the Trump administration’s treatment of Afghan allies could also have long-term consequences for U.S. national security by discouraging people in other countries from working with U.S. forces in future conflicts.
Asked whether the Trump administration was concerned about that, the official said, “I don’t think they care.”

The White House referred a request for comment to the Department of Homeland Security, whose spokesperson said the agency could not confirm removal operations “for operational security reasons.” ICE did not respond to a request for comment.
A State Department spokesperson said the agency had “no plans to announce.”

“We reaffirm our position that all countries must be able to manage their borders and immigration processes in a manner that ensures the safety, security and prosperity of their citizens,” the spokesperson said.
Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment.

The senior administration official said the Afghans on the flight could include people with deportation orders, people who were turned down for asylum and people whose temporary protected status was terminated by the Trump administration. Many of the Afghans facing deportation requested asylum after crossing into the U.S. from Mexico, VanDiver said, and some of their cases are still pending.
‘We just sat there and cried’

Charlotte, a U.S. citizen whose Afghan husband has been in ICE detention since early 2025, said he had been moved to the Louisiana facility from Pennsylvania this month and told he would be deported in early November. She declined to be identified by her full name out of concern that her husband could be targeted by the Taliban.

Charlotte said she and her husband, whose asylum case has been pending for nine years, were visiting family in Maryland last year when he accidentally crossed into West Virginia and was pulled over. Though he was carrying his valid Illinois driver’s license, he did not have his work permit with him.

“When he was pulled over,” she said, “the sheriff actually said, ‘I’m an ICE agent. You’re going to immigration custody. I don’t care if the charges are dismissed, or I don’t care if you have a five-year work permit or Social Security card. I don’t care if you’re legal. Trump’s administration just took over — you’re going directly to immigration custody.’”

Charlotte sold their home in Illinois and moved to Maryland with their son, now 6, in order to be able to visit her husband at the ICE facility where he was held in Pennsylvania, about 100 miles away.
“I lost my nice house, our car, we left everything behind,” she said.
Over the next 20 months, when she took her son to see his father at the Moshannon Valley Processing Center, they were always separated by plexiglass.
“They never let him hug him one time,” Charlotte said. “We just sat there and cried every time.”
But at least they knew where he was and that he was OK, she said. Now that he’s in Louisiana, she said, “we can’t even visit or even say goodbye, he’s over 1,200 miles away.”

With her husband potentially being sent to Pakistan or Afghanistan — a country he hasn’t been to since 2016 — the uncertainty is even greater; Charlotte said he is growing his beard to comply with the Taliban’s strict rules for men’s facial hair.
“I’m just terrified that he’s not going to be safe,” she said, “or he’s going to be held in the jail and there’s nothing I can do.”
Charlotte said she believed her husband had been targeted for deportation because of a past conviction for a nonviolent crime that has since been resolved.
“I still don’t think this should end our entire life, for a child not to see his dad,” she said.
“He’s completely devastated and traumatized,” she said of their son. “He wants to fight. He wants to go protest. He wants to speak to Donald Trump. He basically knows so much more than he should.”

The preparations for the deportation flight come nearly a year after a shooting in Washington that killed one National Guard member and seriously injured another. The suspect, an Afghan national who served alongside U.S. troops in Afghanistan and was evacuated to the U.S. in 2021, had been granted asylum by the Trump administration. Immigration restrictions were tightened after the shooting.

VanDiver said the Trump administration may also be using the Pakistan flight as a test case for Camp As Sayliyah, a U.S.-run camp in Qatar where more than 1,000 Afghans who had been slated for resettlement in the U.S. have been stranded since Trump returned to office last year.

Asked about VanDiver’s claim, the White House referred a request for comment to the Department of Homeland Security, whose spokesperson again said the agency could not confirm removal operations “for operational security reasons.”

According to AfghanEvac, the camp was housing 287 men as of July, 319 women and 433 children. Most of them have been approved for U.S. resettlement after extensive vetting, and many of the adults worked alongside U.S. forces in Afghanistan.
The group at Camp As Sayliyah also includes 150 relatives of U.S. military service members, AfghanEvac said.
Afghan refugees in Qatar protest over travel suspension

The State Department said earlier this year that everyone would be removed from the camp by March 31, a deadline that was later extended to Sept. 30. In September, the Trump administration delayed its closure by another nine months, The Associated Press reported.
Earlier this year, the administration  considered sending the Afghans at Camp As Sayliyah to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which is experiencing the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

In a statement on Friday, AfghanEvac accused the Trump administration of planning the Afghan deportation flight as the country is distracted by next week’s midterm election, “hoping no one is watching.”
“The government won’t say where these flights land, because it knows what happens to the people on them when they do,” the group said. “A government confident in what it is doing does not hide it.”

title: ‘It all happened so fast,’ Oregon educator who confronted school shooter says
summary: The educator as a hero for throwing a cellphone at a teenage gunman in a deadly attack on a Bend, Oregon, elementary school said Friday that “the pain of this loss I will carry with me forever.”
story: The educator hailed as a hero for throwing a cellphone at a teenage gunman during a deadly attack on a Bend, Oregon, elementary school said Friday that “the pain of this loss I will carry with me forever.”
Cassidy Schutz was identified by the school district Friday as the staff member who engaged with the shooter during the attack at Silver Rail Elementary School, which left four people dead.

“There are no words to describe the depth of sadness I am feeling following the events of October 15th. This is not a story. This is a horrific and heartbreaking tragedy, and it is our real lives,” Schutz said in a statement released by Bend-La Pine Schools.
Schutz, a certified learning specialist at the school, was called heroic after she threw her phone at 16-year-old gunman and wrestled him over the shotgun.
An armed community member passing by saw the gunman and followed him into the school, fatally shooting him as he was in the physical confrontation, police have said.

“It all happened so fast, and I wish with everything in me that we had more time,” Schutz said in the statement. “The pain of this loss I will carry with me forever. There are no words for this unimaginable reality we are facing.”

Three boys, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher were killed. Another child and a teacher were wounded. Authorities have publicly identified two of the victims killed as Rhoam Summer, 5, and Megan Lambert, 25.
Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz has said that the educator’s action confronting the gunman “almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The shooting happened in a special needs classroom at the school, officials have said.
“My thoughts are with those who were lost, their families, those who were hurt, and those who were there that day. My heart is with you,” Schutz said.
The shooting remains under investigation and a motive, if one is known, has not been disclosed by officials.
Schutz asked for privacy in Friday’s statement.

title: Selma Blair apologizes to the ‘people that I disappointed’ after plane incident arrest
summary: Selma Blair has spoken out publicly for the first time since her arrest on assault charges after an incident on a plane earlier this month, apologizing to “the people that I disappointed.”
story: Selma Blair has spoken out publicly for the first time since her arrest on assault charges after an incident on a plane earlier this month, apologizing to “the people that I disappointed.”

The 54-year-old “Cruel Intentions” star shared a video on Instagram on Friday, saying that though her attorneys advised her against speaking about the case, she’s taking the legal matter “very seriously.”
“To the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed, I am so sorry,” Blair said.
Actor Selma Blair apologizes after plane incident arrest
In the opening of her video, Blair said, “I know I’ve been quiet for a couple weeks since October 11th, and you deserve to hear from me directly. And I’m sorry that it’s taken this long.”

Blair was on a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York City when she allegedly became “physically abusive” and was removed from the plane, authorities in New York said at the time. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, Port Authority said.

The actor was charged with two counts of second-degree assault related to her alleged actions after the flight. She is accused of kicking a Port Authority police officer who took her to the hospital and a nurse at the hospital later. She pleaded not guilty to those charges.
In her video, Blair defended her character, saying it’s not her nature to harm others.
“What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” Blair said.
She thanked those who reached out with love and support.
“It has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as is Scout, who is also OK,” she said, referring to her service dog.
“So right now, I’m going to be taking care of my health and my son, and thinking of you all with gratitude and love,” she said, concluding her video.

Blair revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disorder that attacks healthy cells in the central nervous system, according to the National Institutes of Health.
Blair’s attorney stated in court that her actions were the result of a medical emergency, citing diagnoses of multiple sclerosis and Parkinsonism.

At her Oct. 12 arraignment, her attorney, Shawn Barnes, told the judge that he doesn’t believe the assault was intentional and that the star had missed several doses of medication and also fell and hit her head on the flight.
Blair’s representative separately said in a statement that Blair had “experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct.”
The case was adjourned until Jan. 19, the DA’s office said.

title: U.S. approves $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine
summary: The Trump administration approved the sale of $2.1 billion in Patriot air defense systems to Ukraine on Friday, the State Department said in a statement.
story: The Trump administration approved the sale of $2.1 billion in Patriot air defense systems to Ukraine on Friday, the State Department said in a statement.
The State Department said 500 Patriot missiles are being purchased for Ukraine with donations from Canada, Germany and Norway through a U.S. program and that no American funds were involved.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe,” the department said in a news release.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said repeatedly in recent weeks that Patriot missile systems are essential for defending against Russian attacks.

“Our soldiers have been very strong this year. Then we really build, try to build air defense shield to defend our civilians, but always a big deficit with Patriot missiles and other kind of air defense,” Zelenskyy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” two weeks ago.
The Ukrainian leader had accused the Pentagon of delaying the delivery of the interceptor missiles that other countries have purchased for Ukraine.
For Subscribers
The announcement of the sale comes as President Donald Trump has recently ramped up criticism of Zelenskyy and described him as an obstacle to efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
For Subscribers
Zelenskyy also recently noted that Ukraine was left further exposed because of restrictions on the Starlink satellite internet service.

Ukraine said Saturday that both Starlink, run by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, and its military variant, Starshield, were fully functional after a long outage, two days after Trump indicated Musk had been asked to “put it back.”

title: DOJ requests separating Alaska ballots that rank Dan J. Sullivan in Senate race
summary: The court filing, which cites the potential for “voter confusion,” did not spell out how segregating ballots would determine if a voter was confused.
story: The Trump administration asked a federal judge Friday to issue an order before Monday directing Alaska election officials to segregate all ballots ranking Senate candidate Dan J. Sullivan as it continues its investigation into his candidacy.

Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote in a court filing that state officials should “preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan for the purposes of investigating whether such ranking was the product of voter confusion, should such an investigation become necessary.”
“These modest precautionary measures will be impossible after Election Day, so there is good cause for expedited consideration,” he added.

The filing did not spell out a process for ballot review or explain how reviewing a ballot would show if a voter was confused about ranking the candidates. Alaska uses ranked choice voting, and there are four Senate candidates on the ballot.

The Trump administration has ramped up its efforts to inject itself into the Alaska election, which by statute is handled by state officials, after The New York Times reported this week that Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan, a former school teacher, to run against Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Peltola has denied any involvement in Sullivan’s campaign.
At a campaign rally Friday evening, Peltola told supporters that she was “so deeply offended by these accusations about having any involvement with anyone else’s candidacy.”

“I want fewer candidates in the primary. I’m not out soliciting more competition,” Peltola said. “I know we can beat Dan Sullivan because every step of the way, even before I got in this race, my poll numbers were higher than his.”
Peltola urged her supporters to get out to vote and encourage those around them, warning that some voters may have been discouraged from voting for her due to the allegations.

“Our work isn’t done yet because we know that there are people out there who have not voted, who don’t have a plan to vote, who are so turned off by the smear campaigns and the garbage, and you know the accusations, the hollow accusations,” she said. “It’s really up to us to remind people why we need to get out and vote.”

Woodward, alongside Alaska’s top federal prosecutor, U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman, made three other filings Friday regarding the civil case the administration is pursuing in hopes of blocking Alaska from certifying the Senate election results.

In one filing, the prosecutors requested expedited sharing of “internal and external conversations” from Peltola’s campaign “regarding its efforts to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan to run for office.” Another filing asks for the “Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee’s internal and external conversations regarding its efforts recruit Daniel J. Sullivan to run for office.”
The DSCC has said it was “not involved with Dan J. Sullivan.”
An additional filing seeks a preliminary injunction in the case.
For Subscribers
Friday’s filings came shortly after Heyman held a press conference in Alaska, where he acknowledged a parallel criminal case.
For Subscribers
Asked what potential crimes prosecutors are looking into, Heyman declined to provide details.

“Because this is an ongoing investigative matter, we can’t discuss the specifics of those investigative steps, and who or may or may not be involved,” he said. “This protects the integrity of the investigation and it protects those who may be the subject or target of those investigations.”
Heyman cited the recent reporting from The New York Times, saying the “new information has resulted in a significant surge of law enforcement assets to Alaska.”
The Justice Department issued at least three dozen new subpoenas and document preservation requests as of Thursday, including subpoenas sent to the campaign offices of Peltola and of Dan J. Sullivan.
President Donald Trump, who has urged legal action against Peltola and the second Sullivan, said Friday morning that he doesn’t know whether Sen. Dan S. Sullivan can win with the current ballot.

“I will tell you, he’s a great senator, and what they tried to do, and he would, you know, he would have won,” Trump said in an interview with Kansas City talk radio host Pete Mundo. “I don’t know how he can win here because you’re splitting up the vote illegally. I think it’s a total fraud.”
Trump has said repeatedly that Dan J. Sullivan should be removed from the ballot.
In an interview with Fox News’ Sean Hannity earlier this week, Sen. Sullivan told supporters in Alaska how to mark up their ballot to best help him on Election Day.

“So rank me first, Sullivan, Dan S. Registered Republican incumbent. That’s what the ballot says,” he said. “Rank the other Republican second, [Gerald] Heikes. Rank, I hate to say it, Sean, but in our screwed-up system, you rank the fake guy third, and then of course blank. Do not rank Peltola. Now that is the screwed up system we have.”

title: The final countdown: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
In today’s edition, we have the latest midterm campaign trail updates from our reporters in the field. Plus, Kristen Welker shares the top Senate races she will be watching Tuesday.
— Adam Wollner
The final countdown

With the midterm elections reaching their conclusion in just four days, NBC News reporters are spread out across the country, speaking with candidates, operatives and voters about the dynamics shaping the biggest races on the map.
Here are our latest dispatches from the campaign trail.

Ohio governor: The fallout from Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign ad featuring the estranged mother of his opponent, Amy Acton, has been a galvanizing moment for Democrats in a state that became redder with President Donald Trump’s rise in politics after a long run as one of the nation’s most competitive battlegrounds, Henry J. Gomez reports from Liberty Township.

A private poll paid for by a Republican group this week showed Ramaswamy trailing Acton by 8 percentage points — a 6-point drop from an earlier survey, said a GOP strategist who works on Ohio races. Similar numbers have rattled around Republican circles for days.

Michigan Senate: During a campaign event for Republican Mike Rogers, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, described Democrat Abdul El-Sayed — who, if elected, would be the first Muslim senator — as “a theocratic zealot” and “jihadist leprechaun” whose election would put American service members at risk because, if presented with national secrets, he would be likely to share them with terrorist groups. Cruz, like other Republicans, sought to link El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, a group the Democrat has condemned.

As Allan Smith writes from Grosse Pointe Woods, Cruz’s message has become a staple of the anti-El-Sayed messaging, with Republicans leaning into the theme in advertising and at campaign events. And they’ve been echoed by some voters.

Georgia governor: While the Southern battleground has two marquee contests on the ballot next week, only the race for the state’s top job between Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms and Republican Rick Jackson remains tight. In the Senate race, polls broadly show Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff with a sizable lead over his Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins.

Bottoms and Jackson both have their eye on winning over a potentially critical slice of the electorate that is supporting Ossoff in the Senate race in the final stretch of the race, Adam Edelman reports from Atlanta. Bottoms has campaigned alongside Ossoff and run ads touting his endorsement, while Jackson has backed away from casting himself as a staunch ally of Trump as he did during his GOP primary.

New Hampshire Senate: Trump has spent nearly every day this month crisscrossing the country to turn out Republican voters in tight Senate races. But he’s steered clear of the Granite State, which he lost in all three presidential contests.

Republican John E. Sununu is reminding the state’s fiercely independent voters that he is not tied to Trump, Brennan Leach and Julie Tsirkin note from Rye. He tells voters in a direct-to-camera TV ad released this month: “I’ve never even met the man!”

Closing message: On the airwaves, Democratic Senate candidates have been far more likely to reference corruption, high costs and Trump, while Republicans have been more focused on immigration, crime and transgender issues. That’s according to an analysis from Bridget Bowman of more than 600 TV ads that launched in October.
The key Senate races I’m watching on election night

Can Democrats turn their recent momentum in red and purple states into a Senate majority? While the battlefield has expanded in recent weeks, here are the races I will be keeping a particularly close eye on next Tuesday.

Michigan: The contest between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers will be a critical test of whether a progressive candidate can win in a swing state as Democrats start to fix their eyes on 2028.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

President Donald Trump won Michigan by less than 1 percentage point in 2024, but voters in a state driven by the auto industry are grappling with high gas prices and costly trade wars with neighboring Canada. Still, Michigan represents one of Republicans’ few pickup opportunities, and if they are able to flip it, that would give them a major boost as they try to maintain Senate control.

Ohio: Sen. John Husted, who was appointed to the seat previously held by Vice President JD Vance, is facing off against former Sen. Sherrod Brown, a Democrat who is on a comeback tour after losing to GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno in 2024.

The race has been affected by the governor’s contest, where Republican Vivek Ramaswamy ran that controversial ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother. The ad, which is no longer running, was met with bipartisan backlash. But could it still serve as a drag on Husted?

Texas: Trump’s endorsement power will be put to the test in the Lone Star State. He ignored concerns from Republicans that GOP Attorney General Ken Paxton would be a weak general election candidate and endorsed him over Sen. John Cornyn in the primary runoff.Since then, Republicans have poured hundreds of millions of dollars into defending the seat. If James Talarico manages to flip it, it will be the first time Democrats have won a Senate seat in Texas in more than three decades.
Despite winning Texas by nearly 14 points in 2024, Trump has made three trips to the state this month alone.

Alaska: There’s a chance control of the Senate could come down to Alaska — and if that happens, it could be several weeks before we know the outcome, given ranked choice voting and the pre-emptive legal challenges developing there.

State and federal investigations are now underway after The New York Times reported that Democratic operatives were involved in recruiting a second Dan Sullivan to appear on the ballot in an effort to pull votes away from incumbent Republican with the same name. Democrat Mary Peltola and her campaign have denied being involved in the effort.

This Sunday on “Meet the Press,” Steve Kornacki will join me to break down the results of the last NBC News poll before Election Day. I’ll also interview Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., the chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee; Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; and Illinois Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker.
🗞️ Today's other top stories

🗓️ Back on: Trump has rescheduled weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa after briefly canceling them yesterday. Read more →📝 Vote watch: The Trump administration has been ordered to turn over its list of 20,000 alleged noncitizen registrants in California to immigrant rights groups by the end of the day, as the Justice Department escalates its legal efforts around the midterms. Read more →🗳️ Ballot battle: Alaska voters will decide next week whether to repeal their ranked choice voting system that has undergone fresh scrutiny amid the controversy around a potential spoiler candidate in the state’s competitive Senate race. Read more →⛪ Papal politics: Pope Leo XIV, a registered voter in Illinois, has voted in the midterms after he requested a mail ballot at his residence in Vatican City. Read more →

That’s all From the Politics Desk for now. Today’s newsletter was compiled by Adam Wollner and Lauren Zola.

title: Meta settles claims with second plaintiff in social media addiction case
summary: Meta on Friday reached a settlement with a teen plaintiff, identified in court documents as K.D.B., who claimed the company’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, were addictive and caused her mental ‌health problems, attorneys for the plaintiff said.
story: Meta on Friday reached a settlement with a teen plaintiff, identified in court documents as K.D.B., who claimed the company’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, were addictive and caused her mental ‌health problems, attorneys for the plaintiff said.

The news comes just one day after the tech giant reached a settlement with S.J., the second teen plaintiff who had sued the company over similar claims. The terms of the settlement agreements with both plaintiffs are confidential.
In the weeks leading up to trial, TikTok and YouTube reached agreements to resolve the claims brought against them by both S.J. and K.D.B.

“We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client,” Emily Jeffcott, trial counsel for K.D.B., said in a statement.
Snap Inc. now remains the lone defendant in the trial, which began this week in Los Angeles with jury selection. Opening arguments are slated for Nov. 4.

In their lawsuit, K.D.B. and S.J. allege that Snap, the maker of Snapchat, designed features that would maximize the time young users spend on the app. Those features include Snapstreaks, Snapscores and filters that can trigger compulsive use of Snapchat, leading to severe mental and physical health issues like self-harm.
Meta settles social media addiction lawsuit for $18 billion

Their case is the fourth bellwether in a consolidated group of cases brought against Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Snap by more than 1,600 plaintiffs, including over 350 families and over 250 school districts. The plaintiffs accuse the tech companies of knowingly designing addictive products harmful to young users’ mental health.

Historically, social media platforms have largely been shielded by Section 230, a provision added to the Communications Act of 1934 that says internet companies aren’t liable for the content users post.
Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, has repeatedly denied that its apps are purposefully harmful and addictive for young users.
In March, during a landmark social media addiction trial in Los Angeles, a jury found Meta and Google’s YouTube negligent in the design or operation of their social media platforms.

The jurors determined that Meta’s and Google’s negligence was a substantial factor in causing harm to the plaintiff, identified in court by her initials, K.G.M., and that the companies failed to adequately warn users of the dangers of Instagram and YouTube, their respective platforms.
The jury awarded K.G.M. $3 million in compensatory damages, finding Meta 70% responsible for harm caused to the now-20-year-old plaintiff, and YouTube responsible for 30%.

In August, Meta agreed to settle a wide-ranging social media addiction lawsuit with the state of California and a number of other states for about $18 billion. The court filing says that the company “denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs,” which are a collection of 29 states.
In a statement to NBC News on Friday, a spokesperson for Meta said the company will continue to defend itself in court and stand by its record.

“We’ve spent more than a decade building protections for teens, and our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general goes even further with strict time limits, no access at night, and no notifications during school hours,” the statement read in part. “We hope the rest of our industry joins us in setting this new standard.”

A spokesperson for Snap on Friday sent NBC News its statement from earlier this week, which read, in part, “From the beginning, Snapchat was built differently from traditional social media: it opens to a camera, not a feed, not a ranking of what other people post or other social comparison metrics.”

“We have built safeguards into the platform, introduced safety tools and educational resources,” the statement continued, “and we believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed.”

title: Appeals court again rejects DOJ’s bid to segregate over 20,000 alleged noncitizen ballots in California
summary: A federal appeals court on Friday rejected the Trump administration’s latest bid to force California to set aside ballots from over 20,000 people it alleges might be noncitizens.
story: A federal appeals court on Friday rejected the Trump administration’s latest bid to force California to set aside ballots from over 20,000 people it alleges might be noncitizens.

The “United States has not made the required showing that such extraordinary relief, during an ongoing election, is clearly required by law,” a 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals panel found in a 2-1 ruling.

“As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system.”
The dissenting judge, Trump appointee Patrick Bumatay, wrote that what the government had been suggesting is a “modest” remedy.

“The federal government and the States can work together. California decided long ago that aliens can’t vote in its elections. Today, the federal government merely seeks to safeguard that decision. We should have let them try,” he wrote.
The majority judges were Mark Bennet, another Trump nominee, and Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden nominee.
It was the second time in a week the appeals court panel had rejected a request from the administration to intervene in the case.
The administration filed suit earlier this month demanding California election officials set aside over 20,000 ballots it contended may have been sent from noncitizens.
In a ruling Wednesday, U.S. District Judge David Carter found the request “violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections.”
“If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he ruled.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Carter also questioned the administration’s methodology in coming up with its list of names, and noted that the Department of Homeland Security had claimed in July that the number of noncitizens who were registered to vote in California was closer to 200,000.

“Given the vagueness of Plaintiff’s descriptions of its procedures and the unreliability of its similar claims in other states, the Court cannot conclude that Plaintiff’s process is credible,” the judge wrote.

He also pointed to similar claims the administration had made in Nevada, where it had alleged there were 15,903 registered voters as noncitizens. They “later reduced that number to 6,218, and then to 185 after conducting its manual review. Nevada officials later confirmed that all 185 individuals were citizens,” the judge wrote.

In its earlier ruling, the appeals court judges also pushed back on the government’s claim it needed to step in on an emergency basis, saying it was “at least in part, a self-constructed one” because it had waited it until far too close to the election to intervene.
The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling or whether it planned to file an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court.

Kristen Clarke, general counsel of the NAACP, which was involved in defending the case, said in a statement, “The Department of Justice sought to throw out the voices of more than 20,000 Californians without credible evidence and outside the established safeguards that protect voters’ rights.”
“Today’s decision sends a clear message: our elections must be governed by facts, law, and constitutional principles, not political interference or voter suppression,” the statement said.

title: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
summary: American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.
story: American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.

Last week’s global release of “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” came days before the Oct. 29 anniversary of the disaster in the South Korean capital’s nightlife district of Itaewon, where a crowd of tens of thousands of partygoers surged beyond control in a narrow alley, causing nearly 160 deaths.

The game, which takes place amid a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, features about 10 seconds of heavily edited footage of the tragedy to illustrate what the aftermath of a Pyongyang attack might look like, though it does not refer to the Itaewon crowd crush directly.

Groups representing families of the crowd crush victims had demanded that the footage be removed, saying it was appalling that the game had directly reproduced actual scenes of people performing CPR “while victims lay on the cold streets amid chaos and desperation.”

“If the game developer has even the slightest sense of respect and empathy for the victims of the Itaewon disaster, it should promptly take corrective action,” the Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee said in a joint statement Friday.
The California-based game publisher, Activision, apologized in a statement and said the footage would be completely removed through a game update scheduled for release Nov. 12.

“This game is a fictional work created to provide a realistic and immersive experience,” the company said, according to the South Korean public broadcaster MBC. “In using actual news footage in the game, we never intended to evoke any tragic incident, including the Itaewon disaster, or to trivialize the suffering associated with such tragedies.”

The controversy came as grieving families are still waiting for answers about authorities’ failure to prevent the disaster four years ago. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged in the investigation, which is still underway, while three former police officers have been jailed.
On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed that his government would “uncover the truth.”

title: Richard Norton, actor and martial artist, died after peptides triggered heart attack, coroner says
summary: Australian actor and martial artist Richard Norton, who faced off in movies against Chuck Norris and Jackie Chan, died of a heart attack tiggered by peptides, according to a coroner’s report.
story: An Australian actor and martial artist who faced off in movies against Chuck Norris and Jackie Chan was felled last year by a heart attack after doubling the dosage of peptides prescribed by his doctor, according to a coroner’s report.
The death of 75-year-old Richard Norton was “was triggered by his injection” of peptides, Melbourne-based coroner David Ryan concluded in a report filed Wednesday in the Coroners Court of Victoria.
“Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner.”

Two days before he died on March 30, 2025, Norton told his doctor’s nurse that “he had been administering double the prescribed dose of CJC1295 & Ipamorelin,” the report states. “The nurse advised Richard that from the following week he ought to only administer the prescribed dose.”
The death of Norton appears to be the first confirmed fatality Down Under linked to unapproved peptides, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported.
Peptides are small proteins that have been promoted by online influencers and others as treatments for everything from faster healing and younger-looking skin to better sleep and even a longer life.

In addition to being a first-class film fighter, Norton also trained Hollywood stars like Ben Affleck, Tom Hardy, Scarlett Johansson and Margot Robbie, and previously worked as a stuntman and bodyguard for rock legends like David Bowie and Stevie Nicks.
Norton was recovering from shoulder surgery when he went to see Dr. Jerzy Muchnicki in March 11, 2025, complaining of fatigue and pain “and advised that he was interested in peptide therapy.”
He admitted to Muchnicki that he’d previously been prescribed peptides by another practitioner to treat similar symptoms.
Muchnicki reviewed Norton’s medical history and “discussed in detail what was involved with peptide therapy, including the experimental nature of the treatment,” the report states.
“They also discussed the potential risks” and Norton signed a consent form before Muchnicki prescribed the peptides, the report states.
Norton, on March 25, “consulted with Dr. Muchnicki and reported that he was feeling good and the peptide therapy was improving his symptoms,” the report states.
On March 28, however, Norton called Muchnicki’s office and told the nurse that he’d “dropped and broken a vial of CJC1295 & Ipamorelin and requested a replacement.”
Norton also told the nurse “he was experiencing better sleep, reduced pain and increased exercise capacity with no side effects.”
“The nurse spoke with Dr. Muchnicki over the phone who authorized the replacement,” the report states.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

That evening, though, Norton’s wife Judy Green called Muchnicki’s office and reported that after administering a second dose of the peptides, her husband “complained of feeling hot and flushed and then collapsed and became unresponsive.”
Norton was rushed to a hospital and two days later he was dead.

In the report, Muchnicki was faulted for authorizing the extra dosage of peptides on March 28 “without consulting the record of a practice nurse, which documented that the patient had reported dosing the medication incorrectly.”
Muchnicki was also taken to task for not speaking directly with Norton “to confirm appropriate use or to assess for potential misuse or adverse effects.”
The doctor, according to the report, has “accepted accountability for his actions” and apologized “for his errors in judgment” and will no longer be prescribing peptides.
NBC News has emailed Muchnicki for comment via his practice. He has not yet responded.

Ryan, in the report, recommended that the Therapeutic Goods Administration, which is Australia’s equivalent of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, impose tougher restrictions on the use of unapproved peptides.
In the U.S., some peptides are used in some medications approved by the FDA to treat diabetes, obesity and other health conditions.
But there is also a “grey market” that has also been flooded with products containing unapproved peptides that are promoted by online influencers and others.

On Wednesday, the Department of Health and Human Services gave compounding pharmacies, which are pharmacies that provide medications that are not commercially available, the okay to start producing six of these much-touted peptides.

They got the green light even though the FDA’s own scientists have concluded there is insufficient data showing these particular peptides — BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500 — are safe and effective.

title: 19+ products we tried and gave our stamp of approval in October
summary: October is when the real holiday shopping starts, and this month we tried new barrel jeans, Jellycat plushies, hairstyling appliances, kitchen accessories and more.
story: While fall technically starts at the end of September it often doesn’t actually feel like it until we’re well into October. Here at NBC Selected, the true signs of fall are easy to spot, not just by a breeze in the air or the crunch of leaves, but by how many seasonal sales take place.

Earlier this month, we wrote about hundreds of deals during fall Prime Day, and even shopped a bunch of them ourselves. Over the course of several sale events — including Target Circle Deal Days and Walmart’s major fall sale — we wrote about, bought and tested products from categories like footwear, beauty, apparel, skin care, appliances and more.
Below, my colleagues and I recommend the products we tested and truly believe are worth sharing. Some of the brands we loved this month include Adidas, Jellycat, Anyday and Bombas.
The best products we tried in October 2026
All of the products below were either sent courtesy of the brand for testing or items that we bought ourselves.
Cory Fernandez, commerce editor
Adidas Handball Spezial Shoes

These shoes have been the ultimate casual sneaker for a few years now and every once in a while I’m inspired to shop for a new color. I recently bought a pair in a brown and white shade that would be perfect to pair with fall fits, including dark-wash jeans and jewel-toned sweaters. They’re comfortable and provide a small amount of arch support, though they’re definitely better suited for weekday commutes rather than long-distance walks. I love that they come with an extra pair of shoe laces and that the laces are long, which makes them easy to double knot. Plus, I enjoy the suede appearance over the leather — something about it feels more cozy and appropriate for this season.
Wine Country Grand Gourmet Gift Basket

Ahead of the holidays and fall hosting season, this brand sent me its marvelous gift basket, which I think is the ultimate gift for a host or anyone you want to say thank you to. It’s filled with tons of salty and sweet snacks, including honey-roasted peanuts, olives, hummus, sesame treats, spreadable cheese and a bunch of international sweets, like mini cakes made in Spain and fruit jellies from Italy. Everything that comes in it would pair well with a rich fall-friendly red wine like a Rioja or Beaujolais, and the brand sells many wine gift baskets as well.
Marilyn La Jeunesse, freelance newsletter editor
Abercrombie Merino Wool-Blend Cardigan

It’s cardigan season, and this Merino wool number from Abercrombie is the perfect amount of plush and chic. While the exact one I received from the brand is now out of stock, this wool-blend option is a comparable alternative — the notable differences are the roll neck and tiny white buttons. Either way, the bright cherry red option is absolutely gorgeous — and an unexpected choice for fall that feels trendy. I’d recommend sizing down if you don’t want an oversized fit.
We can help you find
Gap Curvy High Rise Barrel Jeans

I absolutely hate jean shopping. As someone with an hourglass figure, most jeans leave a massive waist gap, which happens when denim cuts don’t match a higher hip-to-waist ratio. I took a chance on a pair of Gap’s Curvy High Rise Barrel Jeans, ordering them in a 29 petite. I didn’t have high hopes, but I was genuinely shocked when the jeans fit perfectly (and looked good on my body). I love them so much, I bought them in two other colors and will be wearing them on rotation throughout the fall and winter.
Open Farm Icelandic Herring & Salmon Oil For Cats

As my cats age, I’m trying to find them supplements that they’ll actually consume. They’re notoriously picky eaters, which makes it hard to invest in high-end oils without feeling like I’m wasting money. When Open Farm offered to send me a few samples, I knew I wanted to test out their Icelandic fish oil (which they make for both cats and dogs). I started mixing it into their wet food in the mornings and, to my surprise, they’ve actually been eating it. The oil (which doesn’t have any fishy odor) is packed with omegas, which helps joint mobility, skin and coat health and brain function. I feel better knowing that they’re getting a little extra nourishment in every meal.
Jellycat Wizard

When Jellycat invites you to a Halloween party, you go. Dressed as a tired New Yorker (I definitely forgot a real costume), I loved the fully immersive event, complete with donut decorating, a Dylan’s Candy Bar buffet and a massive amount of — you guessed it — Jellycats. This year’s Halloween collection included adorable stuffed bats, gargoyles, peanuts dressed as black cats and so much more. At the end of the night, I was gifted a Rufferty Puppy ‘Wizard’ and an Amuseables Vampop Drink, both of which now sit on my bookshelf and are a welcome addition to my ever-expanding collection of Halloween decor.
Shalwah Evans, senior editor
Adidas Barreda Mary Jane Shoes

At this point, Adidas needs to make me an ambassador because it seems they can’t make a shoe that I don’t like. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin gifted these to me and the second I stepped out of my apartment the first time I wore them, someone said they were “cool-looking” shoes and asked me if they were comfy. And the answer is yes — they’re so comfortable, the break-in was about two hours and that’s only because the leather is a little stiff on the first wear. They’re the ideal commuter shoe for someone who lives in a city like NYC where you ride the train to work, refuse to do it in your heels, but still want to look good. These will probably become my main travel shoes since they’re soft, cozy and come off and back on easily.
Glowissima Ultimate Radiance Face Cream

I got this face cream more than a year ago when it first launched, directly from founders Cynthia Bailey (yep, that Cynthia Bailey) and Dana Hill-Robinson to try it out and I instantly fell in love. It’s a very rich cream but it doesn’t leave my face oily or clog my very large pores. My skin is quite reactive so it will immediately let me know if something is bad or good for it, and this face cream got one of the best responses. It smells nice, it glides on with a smooth creaminess that feels like some luxe brands I’ve used in the past (I’m talking $250 moisturizers), and it absorbs quickly — a huge plus for someone (like me) who carves out very little time from waking up to getting out the door. I recently bought it and used it all up because my skin was very dry from an aggressive treatment I did to get rid of a breakout and this restored its balance in just one month.
Mili Godio, commerce editor
Daphne The Hannah Pant
Daphne The Hannah Long Sleeve

As a longtime Giggler, I’m a huge fan of ‘Bravolebrities’ Paige DeSorbo and Hannah Berner. So, when DeSorbo released the Hannah Collection for her loungewear line Daphne earlier this year, I knew I had to try it out for myself. This set exceeded my expectations: It’s super soft, stretchy and helps replace my usual oversized shirt and sweatpants with something I actually feel cute in. Plus, the matching set and neutral color makes me feel like I have my life together. The pants are definitely too long (I’m 5 foot 3, for reference), but since they’re for lounging, I don’t really mind.
Kiehl’s Creme de Amour Whipped Body Butter

As a beauty editor, I’ve tried my fair share of body creams and lotions, so it takes a lot to impress me. This Kiehl’s body butter, which the brand sent me to try ahead of its September launch, is one of my favorites I’ve used all year. It’s super thick but melts into my skin in minutes, leaving it unbelievably soft and smooth. And I don’t need to use a lot to get the moisture I need, so the tub is going to last me months. There are three body butters in the collection: Creme de Énergique (bergamot and goji berry), Creme de Tranquilitê (black tea) and Creme de Amour (sandalwood and fig). They all smell and feel amazing, but the Creme de Amour is my favorite of the trio; the scent is unmatched, and the light pink color adds a little whimsy to my day.
Ashley Morris, associate reporter, SEO
Dermalogica Clarifying Bacne Spray

Ever since I started taking the gym more seriously, I’ve started experiencing breakouts on my back, which is pretty typical when someone with oily, acne-prone skin like mine begins regularly sweating excessively. So I started using this Dermalogica spray, and the results have definitely paid off. Where I used to constantly have patches of texture, or even bigger, cystic acne bumps, my skin is now smooth, and I only get the occasional breakout or bump or two. I spray it after every shower, and sometimes right after I finish a workout, especially if I’m running errands afterwards — I also like that it helps fade the acne scars on my back a bit as well.
Tower 28 ShineOn Lip Oil Jelly

I started using this lip oil while testing for a story, and as a (self-)certified lip gloss connoisseur, I can say with authority that this is one of the best glosses on the market. It covers all the basic must-haves: hydrating, non-sticky and long-lasting. But what really makes it so great is the color payoff. It’s pigmented enough to wear with a lip liner and a full face of makeup, yet the shade range is wide enough that you can also find the perfect nude for everyday, bare-faced looks. At this point I keep multiple in each bag, but the Coconut shade is definitely one of my favorites.
Jem Alabi, editorial operations associate
Save Khaki United LS Boxy Boat Neck Stripe Tee

Save Khaki United sent me this striped tee to try, and it’s quickly become one of the most-worn tops in my closet. The boxy, relaxed silhouette is incredibly flattering without feeling tight, and the organic cotton, hemp and recycled polyester blend is laundered for an especially soft feel. I’ve washed mine about a dozen times at this point, and it still feels just as good as when I first got it.
Fenty Beauty Gloss Bomb Stix

TikTok made me buy this one. After spotting someone wearing Fenty Beauty’s Gloss Bomb Stix in the shade $weet Whiskey, a rich mahogany color, I immediately added it to my cart, and it has since become my perfect fall lip color. It gives the pigment of a lipstick with the juicy shine of a gloss, but without the sticky feel. The formula also contains squalane, vitamin E and shea butter and is designed to lock in moisture for up to eight hours.
EasyKnit Waffle Relaxed Pullover - Black

There’s something about this sweater that reminds me of the sturdy, well-made knits my parents wore in the ’90s, which is exactly why I love it. It has a relaxed fit and slightly cropped silhouette, but it’s not so short that I have to worry about showing skin. The textured waffle knit makes a simple black sweater feel a little more elevated, and I’ve found it easy to dress up or down. It’s the kind of basic I know I’ll reach for all winter. The brand sent me this sweater to try.
Lador Osmanthus Perfumed Hair Oil

I’m admittedly a sucker for a good-smelling hair product, and the fruity-floral scent is what initially won me over with this Lador oil. It has notes of apricot, jasmine and orris, but there’s more to it than the fragrance: The lightweight formula is designed to add moisture and shine while helping tame frizz and flyaways. I like it so much that Lador’s perfumed shampoo is next on my list to try. Plus, it’s currently part of Ulta’s Early Black Friday sale for $25.20, down from $36.
Lador Tea Tree Calming Scalp Dry Shampoo

This dry shampoo has become such a staple in my morning routine that I keep a travel-sized bottle at my desk. Instead of the powdery formula you may associate with traditional dry shampoo, this is a lightweight, water-based spray that dries transparent without leaving behind any chalky residue or making hair stiff. I especially love using it to help tame my frizz and soothe my dry scalp, and the cooling, fresh feel is an added bonus. It’s also currently 30% off at Ulta, bringing the price down to $15.40.
Muarmus Midnight Leather Jacket

As a K-pop fan, I’m constantly spotting Korean clothing brands I want to try, but getting my hands on them in the U.S. isn’t always easy. That’s what led me to Musinsa, where I found this Muarmus jacket. It was a bit of a splurge, but the rich dark navy color immediately sold me. The faux leather doesn’t look cheap or tacky, the construction feels great and I love the silhouette. It’s become one of my favorite lightweight layers for transitional weather, and I regularly get compliments on both the fit and color.
Zoe Malin, reporter
Duer Performance Denim+ High Rise Barrel Jeans

Ever since Duer sent me these jeans to test, I’ve been ignoring all the other pairs in my closet. They’re made from some of the softest, most comfortable denim I’ve ever worn, and I’ve happily spent 12 hours wearing them — I genuinely don’t want to take them off. I also find their barrel shape flattering. It’s just relaxed enough without feeling baggy or frumpy, and just tailored enough to look chic. I have the dark-wash color, which I prefer for the colder seasons, but there’s a light wash, too. I’ve washed the jeans a few times and they haven’t lost their feel at all.
Ruffwear Sun Shower Dog Raincoat

I’ve had a hard time finding my 1-year-old, 8-pound dog Mabel a raincoat that fits her properly, is easy to put on and take off, and actually keeps her dry. I must have bought and returned at least five options by now — none of them have impressed me. But grandma knows best: My mom bought her Ruffwear’s Sun Shower Dog Raincoat this month and it checks all our boxes. It easily slips over her head and stays put on her body thanks to secure snap-closure straps and leg loops. The coat is a bit longer by the hips and thighs to keep her extra dry, plus it has an extended collar I can fold up to protect her neck from water. I put the raincoat over her harness since it has a leash portal on the back. And best of all, Mabel genuinely enjoys wearing it, and looks adorable in it.
Soma Unbelievable Minimizer Bra

I can’t stand when a bra is advertised as a “minimizer,” yet it doesn’t actually do any minimizing. Thankfully, that’s not the case with this one from Soma, which the brand sent me to test. From the first time I wore it, I noticed that my chest appeared and felt smaller, more secure and smoother under clothes, especially in form-fitting tops, dresses and button-down shirts. The bra is incredibly comfortable, too. It doesn’t dig in or pinch anywhere, and it doesn’t feel restrictive, which is part due to the flexible, unlined mesh cups. I can wear it for hours and practically forget it’s there — that’s the ultimate goal.
Bethany Heitman, commerce editor
Sockerbit Advent Calendar

Growing up, my mom always got us the coolest Advent calendars and I’ve continued the tradition with my own kids. Not wanting to be left out of the fun, I also get my husband and myself one. This year, I chose this Sockerbit option as mine. I had received a PR email months ago alerting me to the fact that the Swedish candy company would be putting one out and made a mental note to order one when they were released — my Spidey senses told me this will be a hot item this year and I didn’t want to miss out. The box is gorgeous and it is filled with two pounds of gummies — including lots of sour options. The hardest part is waiting until Dec. 1 to start opening the doors.
Zafro Smart Dehumidifier

I live in the suburbs of New Jersey, where cave crickets run rampant. Never heard of them? They look like a mix between a dinosaur and a grasshopper. These huge, jumping bugs give me the serious ick and they commonly congregate in basements because they like dark, damp places. One way to mitigate their presence is with a dehumidifier. The one we have in our basement recently broke, so I was on the hunt for a new one. After reading endless reviews, I landed on this model from Zafro. It removes up to 150 pints of moisture daily across 7,500 square feet (great for our large basement) and is Energy Star certified. It’s also quiet and can be controlled via the brand’s app. Since I plugged it in, I haven’t seen a single cave cricket, which is the true win for me.
Bombas Men’s Saturday Suede Boot

I bought these boots for my husband, a man who wears his shoes until there are literal holes in the soles before even considering something new. His feet get freezing cold every winter, so the second I saw these, I knew they were perfect. The plush shearling lining is soft and fuzzy, the cushioned lug sole handles frigid walks to school with our daughter, and they keep him warm in the yard with our son, who insists on playing outside in any weather. Best of all, the silhouette is sleek enough that they never look clunky.
Speks Crags Magnetic Thinking Putty

I love a fidget toy and keep a whole bin of them at my desk for brainstorming sessions or whenever my hands need something to do. Putty is usually my go-to (shoutout to Crazy Aaron’s), but I was intrigued by this magnetic “putty” made of 150+ tiny, matte-coated stones. The little pebbles have such a fun texture when I mush them around in my palm, and they pack neatly into a magnetic tin.
Monica + Andy Soothing Baby Balm

Monica + Andy may be best known for its baby clothes, but the brand just released a line of baby skin care. It sent me the full line to try, and the Soothing Baby Balm was by far the standout. As a mom, I can tell you a good balm is one of the best tools in your baby skin care arsenal. A good formulation soothes irritated patches, helps with dryness and so much more. My 5-year-old has sensitive skin, and when the button on her jeans irritated a spot on her torso, this fragrance-free balm made the redness disappear almost instantly. She’s a tough critic and hates anything that feels greasy or sticky. But she loved this balm and said it made her skin feel “so much better.”
Caitlin Cusack, associate social media editor
Nori Cloud

My old steamer recently broke while I was using it, so I decided it was time to invest in a reliable one. This steamer from Nori is by far the best one I’ve ever tried. It heats up in just a couple minutes and quickly takes all of the wrinkles out of my clothes — I’ve used this on light cotton, denim, heavy sweatshirts and even satin dresses. My favorite part is that the water tank is on the very bottom, so I’m not spilling water everywhere every time I try to refill the tank. It’s also clear, so I can easily see when I need to refill it.
Dyson AirSmooth Styling Brush

As a longtime fan of the similar Revlon One-Step Styling Brush, I was super excited to put the new Dyson AirSmooth Styling Brush to the test. My favorite part about the Dyson brush is the anti-snag bristles that are made completely of rubber. They don’t tug on my hair as much as other brushes I’ve tried, and they do a great job of taming frizz immediately. I’m able to blow out my hair in less than 10 minutes, which is basically half the time of other blow dryer brushes I’ve tried. While $250 is definitely a lot of money for a styling tool, it’s Dyson’s least expensive hair styling product and I think it’s worth it for anyone that styles their hair more than once a week.
Anyday Silicone Clip On Pasta Strainer

Pasta is one of my favorite foods — I probably cook it at least once or twice a week. Before I got this clip-on pasta strainer, I was using a large colander to strain (which definitely wasn’t the easiest thing to store in my tiny NYC kitchen). This is only about 6 inches long, so it can fit in almost any cabinet or drawer. It clips onto the side of your pot and catches the pasta as you pour out the water — so you don’t have to struggle to pour with one hand and hold your colander with the other. It easily drains the water and your pasta stays in the pot you cooked it in. Plus, the silicone material is heat-resistant and dishwasher-safe. I’ve definitely saved a ton of space and time since I got this less than $20 gadget.
Nutrafol Strand Serum

I use a blow dryer brush on my hair around three to four times a week, so I’m no stranger to breakage and split ends. I didn’t realize how much I needed a serum like this until Nutrafol sent me this one to try. It’s lightweight, super potent and does a wonderful job of smoothing out my hair immediately after I apply it. I like to use this right after washing my hair, then again after I style with my blow dryer. My hair always feels so much softer and easier to manage, and after using this for the last few weeks, I’ve genuinely noticed less breakage, fewer split ends and less frizz. The price point is a little steep for a hair serum, but a little definitely goes a long way, so I think that it’s worth the investment since I’ll have this bottle for a while.
Aldo Elanoriaa Tote Bag

Brown is definitely my favorite color to wear during the fall, so I was super excited to try this rich chocolate tote from Aldo. I like to stuff my work bag with a ton of stuff, but hate when it gets too bulky to carry onto the crowded subways and on my walk to the office. This has three large pockets that can fit my water bottle, coffee mug, lunch and more, plus a separate sleeve for my 13-inch laptop. For me, the only thing that’s missing is one or two more internal pockets for smaller things like my keys and work ID. But, for less than $100, this tote is a great pick for anyone that wants a cute, sturdy work bag that won’t bust their budget.
Kailey Sigoda, intern
Franz Early Spot Patch

I recently bought these Franz pimple patches so I could finally stop wearing makeup directly on my breakouts. During Amazon Prime Day earlier this month, I bought the Dr. Melaxin patches, which are known for being ultra-thin and invisible under makeup. After trying both brands, I’ve found they are nearly identical and work great, but Franz does the job at half the price. They are 0.01 millimeters thick, so they easily hide underneath concealer while protecting my blemishes. So far, my breakouts have been healing one to two days faster since I’m exposing them to fewer external irritants.
Beauty Blender Makeup Sponge

These makeup sponges were extremely popular in 2016, and one of the first makeup tools I owned. I’ve been using them practically everyday since to blend out concealer and set my face powder. While I try to wash them regularly, I’ve had my most recent sponge longer than I’d like to admit, so it was time for a fresh one.
Kara Birnbaum, associate art director
Kotn Sanaa Shirt

This shirt is the perfect elevated basic. The structure creates such a nice silhouette and the cropped sleeves make this more interesting than your average button-up shirt. I love the design  and the floral print on top of the stripes is so lovely and takes the shirt to another level. It makes my office outfits more fun while still remaining professional. The brand also says that each purchase allows them to give back to their community in Egypt.
Gap Satin Pull-On Wide-Leg Track-Stripe Pants

I own a pair of pants very similar to these from a much more expensive brand and they are some of my most-worn pants. I thought about buying more but spending upwards of $200 on one pair is not in my budget. These Gap pants fit me the exact same and they even have pockets. I love the stripe down the side and the satin texture — truly the best answer to being casual but also looking cool. They’re such a great alternative for a quarter of the price.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.

Why trust NBC Selected?I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, who writes about home, kitchen and lifestyle products and appliances. I also write about deals and sale events, as well as shopping guides and explainers on retail loyalty programs and memberships. For this column, I reach out to my colleagues at NBC Selected monthly to round up all of the products we tried and recommend.

title: Pokémon Happy Meals Are Coming Back to McDonald’s In a Fun New Way
summary: Pokémon is returning to the Golden Arches just in time for the Japanese franchise’s 30th birthday.
story: Pokémon is returning to the Golden Arches just in time for the Japanese franchise’s 30th birthday.
The limited-time Pokémon Happy Meal at McDonald’s will be available nationwide starting on Nov. 10 and it’s filled with fun goodies, according to The Pokémon Company.

Each meal will come in one of three Happy Meal boxes designed to look like Pikachu, Umbreon or Torchic. The meals will include Pokémon-themed collectible toys and Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) cards.
McDonald’s also announced the new Pokémon Happy Meal Oct. 29 on Instagram, writing, “3 boxes. 15 toys. 2 cards with every collectible. Pokémon Happy Meal coming 11.10.26.”
What’s in the Pokémon Happy Meal?
The Pokémon Happy Meal fans can “catch” will be served in one of three boxes featuring designs inspired by Pikachu, Umbreon and Torchic.
Each box will contain one collectible toy shaped like a small Happy Meal box in the style of various Pokémon characters, including Fuecoco, Sprigatito, Quaxly, Eevee, Umbreon and Bulbasaur.
There are a total of 15 Happy Meal toys in the new collection.
The meals will also feature two Pokémon TCG cards fans can add to their collection. A total of 15 cards will be available to discover, with seven foil cards in the mix.
The new Pokémon Happy Meals will be available for a limited time while supplies last at participating McDonald’s across the country.
Fans of Pokémon on Instagram responded gleefully to the news about the new Happy Meals.
“I’m loving it,” wrote one person, who added emoji of McDonald’s fries and a burger.
“AWWWWWW YEEUH. About to eat an absurd amount of happy meals,” wrote someone else.

Pokémon and McDonald’s have collaborated several times over the decades. Last year, the two companies teamed up on a Pokémon Happy Meal that included Pokémon TCG cards, a Pokémon poster and a sticker sheet.

title: Kylie Jenner Does a Double Take on Lisa Rinna’s Halloween Costume: ‘Thought This Was Me’
summary: Kylie Jenner did a double take when she saw Lisa Rinna dressed as her for Halloween.
story: Kylie Jenner did a double take when she saw Lisa Rinna dressed as her for Halloween.

“Thought this was me,” the youngest Kardashian-Jenner sister joked in the comments of an Instagram post Rinna shared Oct. 30 that showed her re-creating Jenner’s custom Chrome Hearts orange look from the “Marty Supreme” premiere last year.
Rinna, 63, posed in several pics wearing a skin-tight orange dress with cutouts in the torso. She completed the look by wearing a long dark wig, smoky eye makeup and a chunky silver cross necklace.
“King Lisa,” captioned the pics, throwing back to Jenner’s King Kylie era. She added a kiss and crown emoji.
In December 2025, Jenner attended the “Marty Supreme” premiere on the arm of boyfriend Timothée Chalamet, 30, who starred in the film.
Chalamet matched Jenner’s look by wearing an orange Chrome Hearts leather suit and work boots.
The couple previously synched their styles when they both wore all black ensembles during their red carpet debut as a couple at the 70th David Di Donatello film awards in Rome.
Jenner, meanwhile, wasn’t the only one knocked out by Rinna’s spot-on costume.
Hollywood’s biggest Halloween enthusiast, supermodel Heidi Klum, wrote, “Wow” in the comments of Rinna’s post. She added an astonished face emoji.
“Thought it was her for a second,” Rinna’s fellow former Bravo star and “Traitors” alum Dorinda Medley commented, while Rinna’s daughter, model and actor Delilah Belle, wrote, “Wait this is good.”
Over the years, Rinna has re-created other celebrity looks for Halloween.
In 2019, the former “Melrose Place” star won raves when she dressed up as Jennifer Lopez in her early 2000s-era, wearing a replica of J. Lo’s iconic Versace dress.
Like Jenner, Lopez told Access Hollywood she was floored — and flattered —  by Rinna’s tribute to her.
“It was really, really cute,” said Lopez. “She looked awesome.”

story: Live from Central Perk, Phoebe Buffay has released her latest hit single: “Sheinelle-y Cat.”

“Good morning Central Perk, this goes out to all my coffee and kitty lovers out there,” Jenna began.
She then launched into some gloriously off-key singing inspired by the character played by Lisa Kudrow. Phoebe first played the song on a 1995 episode of “Friends.”
“Sheinelle-y cat, Sheinelle-y cat, I love Halloween with you,” Jenna sang. “Sheinelle-y cat, Sheinelle-y cat, you give it your all.”

In her next verse, Jenna referenced Sheinelle’s famous Halloween choreography over the years. Sheinelle took her game to the next level this year as a Rockette and has previously embodied Janet Jackson and Beyoncé.
“Sheinelle-y cat, Sheinelle-y cat, you give it your all,” Jenna sang. “They don’t let me ever dance, they don’t want to take the chance. Sheinelle-y cat, Sheinelle-y cat, kick high but do not fall.”
Far from falling, Sheinelle nailed her Rockettes performance during the costume reveal, with perfect eye-level kicks in sync with the other dancers.

Jenna’s personalized rendition of Phoebe’s song came after Jenna covered the original “Smelly Cat” earlier on TODAY during the Halloween reveal. She and Savannah Guthrie dressed up as Phoebe and Jennifer Aniston’s Rachel Green during a trip through famous NBC moments in honor of the network’s 100th anniversary. Sheinelle strutted into Studio 1A and reprised her dance with a kick line featuring four members of the legendary Rockettes, all decked out in green, red and white for a small taste of the Christmas spirit to come.
